methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Crossbow or Longneck Rifle with Tranquilizer Darts (only needed to clear surrounding threats).; Flying Mount (e.g., Rock Drake, Argentavis, or Lymantria) or Hazardous Environment Suit to maintain elevation and survive poison gas.

inputs.label: Fertilized Voidwyrm Egg (top tier) or Fertilized Rock Drake Egg (standard)

steps.text: Mount up or stand nearby on high ground to locate a wild Basilisk, which usually wanders or remains buried in the ground. Shoot it or drop down near it to pull its aggression, making sure it unburrows and targets you.

Hover above the Basilisk using a flying mount or stand on a nearby ledge out of reach of its melee bites, but close enough to hold its focus. Ensure you have gas protection or keep your distance to avoid its lethal long-range poisonous spit attacks.

Open your inventory and drop a Fertilized Rock Drake or Voidwyrm Egg directly onto the ground near the angry Basilisk. Hover or remain nearby so the Basilisk maintains its aggressive state on you while moving toward your position.

Position yourself so the Basilisk slithers directly over the dropped egg while trying to path toward you. The Basilisk will automatically eat the egg off the ground, gaining a chunk of taming progress; repeat this drop-and-aggro cycle until the tame is complete.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Bola plus Longneck Rifle with Tranquilizer Darts; Crossbow with Tranq Arrows works as a cheaper alternative.; Extra Bolas and Narcotics or Bio Toxin for torpor maintenance if needed. A Bola completely immobilizes a Ravager, making the knockout much easier.

inputs.label: Raw Mutton (preferred) or Cooked Lamb Chop / Raw Prime Meat / Raw Meat

steps.text: Hit your target with a Bola to pin it in place, then immediately begin applying torpor with Tranq Darts or Tranq Arrows. Ravagers can be fully immobilized by Bolas, giving you a clean knockout window.

Ravagers become significantly more dangerous when grouped together, so focus only on the individual you are taming and avoid letting its pack interfere. The pack bonus makes the knockout harder if multiple Ravagers stay engaged.

Keep track of the Bola duration and throw another if the Ravager is still conscious when it breaks free. Do not let it close into melee range while you reload or reposition; keep applying torpor until it drops.

Once the Ravager falls unconscious, access its inventory and load it with Raw Mutton or Raw Prime Meat. Use Narcotics or Bio Toxin if its torpor drops too low, then let it eat until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Catapult Turret with Boulders (recommended), Cannon with Cannon Balls, or Rocket Launcher as an alternative; normal Tranq Arrows and Tranq Darts will not knock it out.; Bring Narcotics or Bio Toxin if needed for torpor maintenance after knockout. Prioritize plenty of Catapult Boulders because missed or poorly placed shots can severely damage the Karkinos instead of building torpor.

inputs.label: followed by Spoiled Meat / Raw Meat / Raw Fish Meat

steps.text: Fire Catapult Boulders directly into the Karkinos's central body to build torpor. Traditional tranquilizers are ineffective; heavy siege impacts are required to force the knockout.

Continue striking the body with Boulders until the Karkinos collapses. Catapults are generally preferred over Cannons because they apply roughly 400 torpor per hit and give you much better control over the knockout.

Do not hit the legs or claws—limb shots deal heavy health damage instead of properly applying torpor and can easily kill the Karkinos. Cannon shots are especially unforgiving, so accurate body hits are critical.

Once the Karkinos falls unconscious, access its inventory and load it with Exceptional Kibble. Keep an eye on its torpor and use Narcotics or Bio Toxin if necessary until the taming meter reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None; Lampreys are torpor-immune and cannot be knocked out for taming.; Fish Basket. Place the basket on the ground underwater near the Lamprey and wait for it to enter capture range.

inputs.label: None; Lampreys are captured directly with a Fish Basket and require no Kibble

steps.text: Set a Fish Basket underwater near the Lamprey and allow it to swim close enough for the capture prompt to appear. Do not use tranquilizers—the Lamprey is immune to torpor.
When the Lamprey enters the basket's capture range, interact with the Fish Basket to trap it. This functions as the Lamprey's taming method and stores the creature inside the basket for transport.

Lampreys are aggressive and may attack and attach to you while you are positioning the basket, potentially wasting the capture attempt. Keep out of their direct path and trigger the basket interaction as soon as one moves into range.

Deploy the filled Fish Basket back into water to release the Lamprey as a tribe-owned creature. No feeding phase follows, but the tame is effectively one-use—once a Lamprey successfully latches onto a target, it is permanently lost afterward.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None required; the Featherlight is a non-violent passive tame.; Place your taming food in the very last slot of your hotbar. A Charge Lantern can optionally force a flying Featherlight to land without damaging it.

inputs.label: Plant Species Z Seed (preferred) or Auric Mushroom

steps.text: Put Plant Species Z Seeds in your last hotbar slot and approach the wild Featherlight. When the interaction prompt appears, press the interaction key (E) to feed it one seed.
After each feeding, the Featherlight must become hungry again before accepting another. Stay close and follow it as it walks or flies around until the feeding prompt returns.

Do not attack, tranquilize, or accidentally damage the Featherlight; taking damage causes it to fly away and can make continuing the tame difficult. If it keeps taking flight, a Charge Lantern can safely stun it out of the air and force it to land.
Continue feeding Plant Species Z Seeds each time the prompt becomes available. Once the taming meter reaches 100%, the Featherlight is immediately tamed—no knockout or inventory feeding is required.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None required; the Shinehorn is a non-violent passive tame and should not be damaged.; Place the preferred food in the **last slot of your hotbar**. No Narcotics or torpor-maintenance items are required.

steps.text: Walk up to the wild Shinehorn without striking or tranquilizing it. It is passive and will not fight back, but damaging or frightening it can make it flee.
With a Plant Species Z Seed in your final hotbar slot, move close enough for the feeding prompt and press the interaction key (E). The first feed immediately begins the passive-taming process.
Stay close while waiting for the Shinehorn to become hungry again, but avoid attacking it or allowing nearby threats to send it running. Simply follow and watch for the feeding prompt to return.

Feed another Plant Species Z Seed every time the interaction becomes available. Continue the passive-feed cycle until the taming bar reaches 100%, at which point the Shinehorn immediately becomes yours.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None; Glowtails are passive tames and should not be knocked unconscious.; Place the preferred taming food in the very last slot of your hotbar so you can hand-feed it when the interaction prompt appears.

steps.text: Walk up to the wild Glowtail with its taming food in your last hotbar slot. Do not shoot or tranq it; this is a non-violent passive tame.
When the interaction prompt appears, press the interaction key (E) to feed it. Plant Species Z Seeds give the best taming progress, while Ascerbic Mushrooms are the best common alternative.
You cannot feed a Glowtail while it is swimming or standing in water. If it wanders into water, wait for it to come out or carefully move it onto dry ground before attempting the next feed.

Wait for the Glowtail to become hungry again, then feed it each time the interaction prompt returns. Continue the feed-and-wait cycle until the taming meter reaches 100% and the Glowtail becomes yours.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None required (Passive Tame).; None required. Ensure your taming food is placed in the far-right slot of your hotbar (slot 0).

steps.text: Place your chosen taming food into the last slot of your action bar. Approach the wild Bulbdog quietly from behind or the side to avoid startling it.
Walk directly up to the creature until the prompt "Feed [Food] to Tame" appears above its head. Press the interaction key (E) to hand-feed it a single unit of food.
Track the Bulbdog as it wanders randomly around the area. Wait for its hunger to drop enough for the next feeding prompt while keeping local predators away from the fragile creature.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None required; the Roll Rat uses a unique passive-taming mechanic and should not be attacked or knocked out.; Giant Bee Honey placed in the very last slot of your hotbar. Bring extra Honey because thrown pieces cannot be recovered if you miss the burrow.

steps.text: Follow the wild Roll Rat without attacking it and watch for it to dig underground. When its tail is sticking up from the burrow, aim directly at the hole and use the Giant Bee Honey from your last hotbar slot to throw it in.
After eating the Honey, the Roll Rat will emerge and resume wandering. Keep following it and throw another Honey into the hole each time it performs a genuine burrow until the taming meter fills.

phases.name: Do Not Fall for Fake Digs

steps.text: The Roll Rat sometimes begins digging only to unearth gems instead of presenting a feeding opportunity, so wait until its tail is visibly sticking from the hole before throwing Honey. Never steal the gems or let the Roll Rat enter combat—combat completely resets its taming progress and effectiveness.

Continue throwing Giant Bee Honey into each valid burrow until the taming meter reaches 100%. The Roll Rat immediately becomes yours after the final successful feeding; there is no knockout or inventory-feeding stage.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Harpoon Gun with Tranq Harpoon Bolts (underwater) or Longneck Rifle with Tranquilizer Darts.; Scuba Gear or Lazarus Chowder for oxygen maintenance, along with Narcotics or Bio Toxin for torpor management. Place taming food in the last slot of your hotbar if utilizing passive intervals.

steps.text: Locate the Abyssal Ankylosaurus in deep trench waters and clear out surrounding marine predators like Megalodons or Electrophorus. Use a Harpoon Gun loaded with Tranq Bolts to begin building up its torpor before it can draw close.

Maintain distance while firing consistently, taking advantage of its relatively slow swimming speed. Keep an eye on its torpor meter—if it reaches a high threshold, the creature will attempt to flee rapidly toward deeper trenches or hostile terrain.
Stay out of range of its heavy tail sweep, which inflicts massive physical damage and can drain your stamina rapidly underwater. Never approach head-on while it is actively hostile,
Once the Abyssal Ankylosaurus is completely knocked out and sinks to the seabed, open its inventory immediately. Insert

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Harpoon Gun (with Tranq Harpoon Bolts) or Crossbow (with Tranq Arrows).; Scuba Gear (specifically Scuba Tank and Flippers) or Lazarus Chowder, Bio Toxin or Narcotics, and a Water mount for protection/positioning.

steps.text: Locate the Abyssal Moschops in the deep ocean/trench regions and lure it away from aggressive aquatic predators like Megalodons or Tusoteuthis using a fast water mount.

Unlike its timid terrestrial counterpart, the Abyssal variant becomes aggressive when underwater; maintain a safe distance using Scuba Flippers and shoot it continuously with Tranq Harpoon Bolts to rapidly build torpor.

Watch for the Abyssal Moschops to tilt back and generate a blue bioluminescent wave. Immediately swim backward out of range to avoid its underwater directional pulse, which will dismount, stun, and drain your oxygen rapidly if hit.

Continue applying torpor until the creature attempts to flee and eventually falls unconscious to the seabed. Once KO'd, clear the immediate area of predators, access its inventory, and insert Giant Bee Honey or Superior Kibble alongside Narcotics to complete the taming bar.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Harpoon Gun (for Net Projectile) or High-Quality Crossbow/Longneck Rifle.; Bug Repellant and SCUBA Gear (to survive deep ocean depths and avoid unwanted aggro).

steps.text: Locate the Abyssal Procoptodon in deep water, clear surrounding predators, and pin it using a Net Projectile to stop its fast swimming and leaping.
Shoot it with Tranq Darts or Tranq Arrows while immobilized until its torpor maxes out and it drops unconscious.
Keep a close watch on its oxygen meter while down, as underwater knockout tames can drown if oxygen depletes fully before taming completes. Use Narcotics or Bio Toxin to maintain torpor as needed.
Access the unconscious creature's inventory and load it with Exceptional Kibble, Plant Species Y Seeds, or Rare Mushrooms to fill the taming bar and finalize the tame.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: High-quality Crossbow or Longneck Rifle loaded with Tranquilizer Arrows, Tranquilizer Darts, or Shocking Tranquilizer Darts.; Narcotics or Bio Toxin to maintain torpor levels while unconscious.

steps.text: Position yourself on elevated terrain or at a safe range away from the Abyssal Rex's dangerous melee zone. Fire tranq projectiles continuously into its head to inflict maximum torpor per shot.

Continue to land successive shots as the creature charges and attacks. Keep a close eye on its movement patterns—once its torpor reaches roughly 80–90%, the Abyssal Rex will stop attacking, turn around, and attempt to sprint away in a panic.

Chase after the fleeing Abyssal Rex to maintain line-of-sight and keep re-applying torpor before its meters start draining. Fire your final shots until it collapses to the ground in a unconscious state.

Immediately clear the surrounding zone of any local aquatic or land predators to protect the unconscious target. Open the Abyssal Rex's inventory, load it with Exceptional Kibble or Raw Mutton, and feed Narcotics or Bio Toxin as needed until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: High-quality Crossbow or Longneck Rifle with Tranq Arrows/Darts (Standard KO tame mechanic).; Bio Toxin or Narcotics/Narcoberries to keep torpor high during the tame.

steps.text: Locate the Abyssal Stegosaurus in deep/abyssal zones and draw its attention using a ranged weapon. Maintain a safe distance, as its slow speed makes it exceptionally easy to kite on foot or from a high cliff/mount.

Pay attention to its current plate mode during the chase. If it activates its Hardened Plate stance, it will take reduced damage and lower torpor, so continue cycling shots while keeping your distance to drain its health and raise its torpor efficiently.

Keep firing tranquility projectiles into its body or head while avoiding its wide tail-sweep attacks. Watch its torpor bar carefully and avoid shooting too quickly once its health drops dangerously low to prevent accidental death.

Continue shooting until the Abyssal Stegosaurus is rendered unconscious. Once down, immediately place Regular Kibble, Crops, or Mejoberries into its inventory alongside Narcotics or Bio Toxin to complete the taming process.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: High-quality Longneck Rifle with Shocking Tranq Darts or Tranq Darts (Crossbow with Tranq Arrows works as a budget option).; Bio Toxin or Narcotics (hundreds required due to rapid torpor drain). Keep these in your main inventory for force-feeding.

steps.text: Target the Abyssal Therizinosaur from a safe elevated position or ledge to avoid its devastating melee attacks. Fire your Tranq Darts in steady, timed intervals to maximize torpor buildup without risking accidental death.

Maintain distance as the creature takes damage; it maintains high movement speed and relentless aggression while torpor builds. Keep shooting as it attempts to charge, and be prepared to reposition quickly if it paths up high terrain toward you.

As soon as the Abyssal Therizinosaur drops unconscious, open its inventory immediately and feed it a heavy stack of Bio Toxin or Narcotics. Its torpor drains at an extremely high rate, meaning you must constantly monitor and force-feed torpor items throughout the process to prevent it from waking up early.
Place Exceptional Kibble or crops into its inventory immediately after stabilizing its torpor bar. Protect the unconscious creature from nearby predators until the taming meter reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: High-damage Longneck Rifle with Tranquilizer Darts or Shocking Tranquilizer Darts.; Scuba Gear (or Lazarus Chowder), Bio Toxin or Narcotics, and a Harpoon Gun with Net Projectiles (if immobilizing first).

steps.text: Locate the Abyssal Thylacoleo swimming or lurking near deep underwater rock faces and isolate it from surrounding aquatic predators. Shoot it with a Longneck Rifle or net it with a Harpoon Gun to freeze its position and prevent it from swimming into dangerous depths.

Maintain your distance while underwater using Scuba Gear, as the Abyssal Thylacoleo possesses rapid swimming speed and can dismount you instantly if it lunges. Rapidly apply torpor using Shocking Tranq Darts while tracking its underwater movement.

Watch for a tail-thrashing animation when its torpor gets high, signaling a desperate retreat straight toward the seafloor or nearby underwater crevices. Do not let it wedge itself into geometry or drag you into deep-sea threats like Tusoteuthis or Alpha predators.
Continue firing darts until the creature drops unconscious to the ocean floor. Access its inventory underwater,

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: High-quality Crossbow or Longneck Rifle loaded with Tranq Arrows or Shocking Tranq Darts.; Large Bear Traps (optional for immobilization), Bio Toxin, Narcotics, or Narcoberries to sustain its fast-depleting torpor pool.

steps.text: Locate the target Yutyrannus and immediately pick off its accompanying Carnotaurus pack from long range before engaging. Attempting to initiate the knock-out sequence while the Carnotaurus minions are active will result in heavy damage and constant fear-buffed aggression.

Shoot the Yutyrannus using your chosen tranq weapon while positioning yourself on high, steep terrain or an elevated ledge. Watch out for its distinct Courage and Fear Roars; if you are on a mount that isn't immune to fear, the Yutyrannus will force your mount to flee out of control and disrupt your continuous torpor stack.

Track the Yutyrannus closely once its torpor threshold reaches approximately 75% and it begins fleeing uncontrollably. Keep up continuous shots to prevent its torpor from dropping, taking care not to lead it into neighboring predators or hostile biomes.

Continue firing until the creature collapses into unconsciousness. Once down, immediately access its inventory, load it with Exceptional Kibble or Raw Mutton, and feed it Bio Toxin or Narcotics regularly to counter its high torpor depletion rate until fully tamed.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Harpoon Gun loaded with Net Projectiles, high-quality Crossbow or Longneck Rifle.; Scuba Gear (Oxygen and Flippers recommended), Bio Toxin or Narcotics, and a fast underwater mount (Baryonyx or Megalodon).

steps.text: Locate the Chrysaora in deep open water and dispatch any surrounding ocean predators to avoid interference. Fire a Net Projectile from your Harpoon Gun to trap the jelly-like creature and prevent it from drifting or attacking.

Maintain distance to avoid its shocking tentacles and fire Tranq Arrows or Tranq Darts directly into its main bell structure while net-trapped. Keep a steady firing cadence without rushing, as hitting its tentacles will deal reduced damage and torpor.

If the net wears off before knockout, backpedal rapidly using your Scuba Flippers or underwater mount to avoid its high-damage shock attacks, which can dismount and stun you. Re-apply a Net Projectile immediately if it begins floating rapidly toward you in an aggressive state.

Continue applying torpor until the Chrysaora floats down to the ocean floor unconscious. Access its inventory instantly, insert Superior Kibble or Raw Prime Meat, and monitor its torpor level using Bio Toxin until the taming bar fills.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Harpoon Gun loaded with Tranq Harpoon Bolts, or high-quality Longneck Rifle / Crossbow with Tranq Darts / Arrows.; Scuba Gear (Oxygen tank and Flippers are essential), Water Mount or Grappling Hooks, and Narcotics / Bio Toxin for torpor maintenance.

steps.text: Locate the Dakosaurus in deep aquatic ocean areas and lure it away from aggressive underwater packs like Megalodons or Plesiosaurs. Ensure you are wearing Scuba Gear or riding a strong water mount to maintain mobility and breath.

Shoot the Dakosaurus with your tranquilizer weapon from range to draw aggression. When it closes the distance, it will attempt a signature lunging barrel-roll attack; evade laterally using your flippers or mount to avoid massive burst damage and bleed effects.

Turn and shoot it with Tranq Harpoon Bolts or Darts immediately after it finishes its attack animation while it turns around to target you again. Keep sufficient distance during its recovery window to safely accumulate torpor without getting cornered.
Continue the kite-and-shoot cycle until the Dakosaurus goes unconscious and floats in the water column. Access its inventory while monitoring its torpor, insert Superior Kibble or Raw Mutton,

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Catapult Turret with Boulders (recommended) or Cannon with Cannon Balls; normal Tranq Arrows and Tranq Darts will not knock it out.; Bring Narcotics or Bio Toxin for torpor maintenance after knockout. Homarus uses the same specialized knockout mechanic as Karkinos.

inputs.label: followed by Spoiled Meat / Raw Meat / Raw Fish Meat

steps.text: Fire Catapult Boulders directly into the Homarus's central body to build torpor. Conventional tranquilizers are ineffective for this mechanic; heavy siege impacts are what force the knockout.

Continue striking the body with Boulders until its torpor reaches the knockout threshold. A Catapult is generally safer than a Cannon because it gives you more controlled torpor buildup without dealing excessive damage.

Do not hit the Homarus's legs or claws—like Karkinos, limb hits deal heavy health damage instead of properly applying torpor and can kill your target. Also stay clear of its enlarged claws, which can grab and immobilize a survivor during the attempt.

Once the Homarus collapses, immediately access its inventory and load it with Exceptional Kibble, using Narcotics or Bio Toxin if its torpor begins falling too far. Let it eat naturally until the taming meter reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Dipping Net; no tranquilizer weapons are required.; Dipping Net Ammo. Bring several pieces because each capture attempt can fail, and failed attempts reduce the Dipping Net's durability.

inputs.label: None. Istiophorus is captured directly with a net rather than knocked out and fed

steps.text: Swim directly toward the Istiophorus with your Dipping Net equipped. Get within the net's short capture range without attacking the fish.

Use the Dipping Net when you are close enough to catch the Istiophorus. Successful net captures convert the targeted fish into a contained tame rather than starting a traditional knockout or passive-feeding process.

Istiophorus is defensive and can stab or bite when threatened, so avoid damaging it while positioning for the capture. If the net attempt fails, immediately reposition and try again before it gets away; failed attempts also cost Dipping Net durability.

Keep making close-range net attempts until the Istiophorus is successfully captured. No Narcotics, Kibble, knockout timer, or follow-up feeding phase is required—the net capture itself completes the tame.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None. Do not use tranquilizers or damage the Kathreptis; it is a passive tame.; Black Pearls. Place them in the very last slot of your hotbar before approaching.

inputs.label: Black Pearls exclusively; expect multiple feedings to complete higher-level tames

steps.text: Swim close to the wild Kathreptis with Black Pearls in your last hotbar slot. Wait until the passive-feed interaction prompt appears, then press the interaction key (E) to give it a Black Pearl.
After each Black Pearl, stay near the Kathreptis and wait for it to become hungry again. Move back into interaction range as soon as the feeding prompt returns and feed another Pearl.

Kathreptis is naturally skittish and attempts to flee from danger, so do not attack it or turn the tame into a torpor attempt. Follow it carefully if it swims away and continue feeding only when the interaction prompt is available.
Repeat the Black Pearl feedings until the taming bar reaches 100%. The Kathreptis will automatically become yours—no knockout, Narcotics, inventory feeding, or final claim interaction is required.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Spear, Crossbow, or aquatic combat tame for quickly killing fish; do not attack the Mantis Shrimp itself.; No Narcotics or knockout supplies required. You must be able to drag freshly killed fish corpses to the Mantis Shrimp; Monodon Horns are also supported as an alternative taming resource.

inputs.label: preferably larger fish for better taming progress; Monodon Horns can also be used

steps.text: Find a wild fish near the Mantis Shrimp and kill it without damaging your intended tame. Leave the corpse intact rather than harvesting it.

Grab the dead fish and physically drag its body to the Mantis Shrimp, similar to taming a Hesperornis. Bring the corpse close enough for the shrimp to accept and consume it, increasing the taming bar.

Do not attempt to hand-feed or attack the Mantis Shrimp; it is territorial and its powerful punch can punish careless approaches. Deliver the offering, give it room, and repeat with additional fresh fish instead of trying to force-feed it.

Continue killing fish and dragging their corpses to the Mantis Shrimp until its taming progress reaches 100%. No knockout or inventory-feeding phase follows—the successful corpse offerings complete the passive tame.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None required; the Monodon is a non-violent ride-to-tame creature and uses its own horn to spear fish during the taming process.; No external taming items are required. Mount the wild Monodon directly and use its secondary attack after spearing fish to consume them and gain taming progress.

inputs.label: Small wild fish speared with the Monodon’s horn; larger fish provide more taming progress. Piranhas do not count and cannot be used

steps.text: Swim directly up to the Monodon and interact with it to climb onto its back, similar to mounting a wild Equus. Once mounted, you gain control of its movement and can begin the taming sequence.

Swim into small fish and spear them using the Monodon’s horn, stacking up to three fish before feeding. Then use the secondary attack to make the Monodon consume the impaled fish; feeding three together gives substantially more taming progress and reduces the number of feedings required.

Every time the Monodon consumes fish, a three-minute timer begins. Catch and feed another batch before it expires; failing the timer interrupts the tame, forces you to remount the Monodon, and causes taming progress to drop.

Continue spearing the largest available fish, preferably three per feeding, and immediately consume each batch with the secondary attack. Keep the feeding chain active until the taming meter reaches 100%, at which point the Monodon becomes yours without a knockout or traditional inventory-feeding stage.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None required; the Mudpuppy is a non-violent passive tame and should not be tranquilized or damaged.; Place your chosen food in the **last slot of your hotbar** and keep extra feeds ready; the Mudpuppy must become hungry again between each interaction.

inputs.label: followed by Raw Prime Fish Meat or Raw Fish Meat at lower effectiveness

steps.text: Walk up to the wild Mudpuppy without shooting, striking, or attempting to knock it out. When you are close enough, the passive-feed interaction prompt will appear.
With Basic Kibble or Earthworms in your final hotbar slot, press the interaction key (E) to feed the Mudpuppy. Each successful feed increases its taming progress.

phases.name: Wait for It to Get Hungry

steps.text: Do not spam the interaction key or attempt to force additional food immediately after a feed. The Mudpuppy has a feeding cooldown, so stay nearby and wait patiently until the interaction prompt returns.
Feed it again every time it becomes hungry and continue the passive-feed cycle until the taming bar reaches 100%. Once the final feed completes the bar, the Mudpuppy immediately becomes yours.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None. Ocepechelon is a passive tame and should not be damaged during the taming process.; Multiple Filled Fish Baskets. Place a Filled Fish Basket in the very last slot of your hotbar before approaching.

inputs.label: Filled Fish Basket. Ocepechelon does not use Kibble

steps.text: Swim up to the wild Ocepechelon without damaging it. It is normally defensive rather than immediately aggressive, allowing you to approach for the passive tame.
With a Filled Fish Basket in your last hotbar slot, move within interaction range and press the interaction key (E) when the feeding prompt appears. Each successful feeding adds taming progress.

phases.name: Wait for It to Get Hungry

steps.text: You cannot rapidly feed all required baskets at once. After each feeding, stay near the Ocepechelon and wait until it becomes hungry enough for the interaction prompt to return; attacking it is unnecessary and can turn the encounter hostile.

Continue feeding Filled Fish Baskets whenever the prompt becomes available until the taming bar reaches 100%. The Ocepechelon will automatically become yours after the final feeding—no knockout, Narcotics, or inventory feeding is required.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Crossbow with Tranq Arrows, Harpoon Launcher with Tranq Spear Bolts, or a Thalassian Rifle with Tranq Thalassian Ammo for efficient underwater torpor.; Narcotics, Bio Toxin, or Narcoberries for torpor maintenance after knockout. Bring enough ammunition to handle its **600 base torpor plus 36 per wild level**.

steps.text: Attack the defensive Onchopristis with your underwater tranq weapon to make it engage. Keep moving while landing controlled torpor shots; its long saw-like rostrum makes fighting directly in front of it dangerous.

Strafe around its sides and continue applying torpor while it attempts to close distance. Maintain enough separation to avoid its exposed teeth and saw attacks while keeping consistent shots on target.

Avoid sitting directly in its charge path or trying to tank its attacks while firing. Its wild attacks can apply a debuff that causes you to take increased ranged damage, so prioritize movement until the torpor finally drops it.

Continue applying torpor until the Onchopristis falls unconscious, then immediately access its inventory and load it with Superior Kibble or fish meat. Monitor its torpor and force-feed Narcotics or Bio Toxin as needed until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Dipping Net; do not use tranquilizers or damage the Qarmoutus.; Dipping Net Ammo loaded into the Dipping Net. Bring several pieces because capture attempts can fail and failed swings damage the net.

inputs.label: None. Qarmoutus is captured directly with a Dipping Net rather than knocked out or fed

steps.text: Equip the Dipping Net and swim directly toward the Qarmoutus. Get within the net's short capture range without attacking it.
Use the Dipping Net while the Qarmoutus is within reach. A successful attempt immediately catches the fish and converts your net ammo into a Filled Dipping Net containing the Qarmoutus.

Capture attempts have a chance to fail, and the Qarmoutus is skittish and may swim away when approached. Keep chasing and make controlled close-range swings; failed attempts reduce the Dipping Net's durability.

Continue attempting the capture until the Qarmoutus is successfully caught in the Filled Dipping Net. The capture itself completes the domestication process—no knockout, Narcotics, Kibble, or passive-feeding phase is required.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Longneck Rifle with Tranquilizer Darts or Crossbow with Tranq Arrows; the Riftcrawler uses a standard knockout tame and has **800 base torpor plus 48 per wild level**.; Narcotics, Bio Toxin, or Narcoberries for torpor maintenance after knockout. Bring plenty of tranquilizer ammunition for higher-level Riftcrawlers.

inputs.label: then other Berries; the Riftcrawler is a herbivore

steps.text: Hit the Riftcrawler with Tranq Darts or Tranq Arrows to begin the knockout. Once attacked, its defensive temperament causes it to fight back, so immediately create distance and continue landing controlled shots.

Continue firing tranquilizers until its torpor reaches the knockout threshold. The Riftcrawler has no special passive or interaction-based taming mechanic; it is explicitly classified as a **knockout tame**.

Do not stand directly beside the Riftcrawler while applying torpor. Its stone-and-metal body makes it a durable defensive creature, so maintain range and avoid unnecessary damaging shots while building the torpor you need.

Once the Riftcrawler falls unconscious, immediately access its inventory and load it with your best available herbivore food. Monitor its torpor and force-feed Narcotics, Bio Toxin, or Narcoberries as needed until the taming bar reaches 100% and the Riftcrawler wakes up tamed.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Crossbow with Tranq Arrows (recommended underwater) or Harpoon Launcher with Tranq Spear Bolts.; Narcotics or Bio Toxin for torpor maintenance if needed. The Seahorse is a standard knockout tame despite its unusual Aquatica abilities.

inputs.label: followed by Crops / Mejoberries / other Berries

steps.text: Shoot the Seahorse with Tranq Arrows or Tranq Spear Bolts until its torpor begins climbing. Keep your shots controlled and centered on the body while staying within underwater firing range.

Continue applying torpor as it swims away or turns defensive. It has a base torpor of 300 and gains additional torpor with level, so higher-level individuals require substantially more tranquilizer hits.

Do not sit directly in front of the Seahorse while trading shots; wild Seahorses can spit acid at enemies. Keep repositioning between tranq shots and stop firing immediately once it collapses to avoid unnecessary damage.

Once the Seahorse falls unconscious, access its inventory and load it with Regular Kibble or your best available herbivore food. Maintain torpor with Narcotics or Bio Toxin as necessary and let it eat naturally until the taming meter reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None for the tame itself; bring a weapon only to eliminate nearby hostile creatures before starting, as combat can interrupt the taming sequence.; No tranquilizers or Narcotics required. Keep your chosen fish food ready for the feeding phase and use nearby terrain or cover to break the Tiktaalik's line of sight during its hide-and-seek game.

inputs.label: Raw Prime Fish Meat or Prime Fish Jerky (preferred)

steps.text: Approach the wild Tiktaalik and use the interaction prompt to begin taming. It will cover its eyes and start a **30-second countdown**; immediately hide nearby where it cannot see you, but stay within roughly 100 meters.

Successfully remain hidden through the first countdown and the Tiktaalik will uncover its eyes and spend about **30 seconds searching** for you. Whether it finds you early or the search timer expires, it will then approach and hold its mouth open, signaling that it is ready to be fed.

phases.name: Do Not Fail the Hiding Phase

steps.text: Do not remain visible or move more than roughly 100 meters away while it is counting; either mistake interrupts that round and costs taming effectiveness, typically around 10% per failure. Keep hostile creatures away as well, because outside aggression can interrupt the game.

Feed the Tiktaalik fish when it approaches with its mouth open. It will cover its eyes again and restart the hide-and-seek cycle; repeat the **hide → search → feed** sequence until the taming bar reaches 100% and the Tiktaalik becomes yours.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: High-damage Pump-Action Shotgun or Fabricated Sniper Rifle.; Bio Toxin (recommended for higher torpor gains and self-healing), or Narcotics/Narcoberries. Place these in the very last slot of your hotbar.

inputs.label: Exceptional Kibble (preferred) or Raw Mutton / Raw Prime Meat

steps.text: Shoot the wild Acrocanthosaurus with your shotgun or rifle. After taking enough damage (around mid-health), it will enter a sideways-walking "shield stance" that drastically reduces incoming damage.

Keep shooting it while it is in its shield stance. Eventually, it will perform a distinct, loud roaring animation and open its mouth. Immediately run up to its open mouth and press the interaction key (E) to feed it 5 units of Bio Toxin or Narcotics from your last hotbar slot. This will briefly interrupt the roar, raise its torpor, and heal the Acro back up to full health.

Beware of "fake roars" or stagger animations which can bait you in and stun you; only approach when it executes the proper feeding roar. If you miss the window or move too far away, it may enter an aggressive adrenaline state requiring you to survive and re-engage.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Harpoon Gun or Crossbow (for clearing aquatic threats only; do not shoot the Archelon directly).; Scuba Gear (tank and flippers required for deep-sea maneuvering) and Bio Toxin (placed in your last hotbar slot).

steps.text: Find the wild Archelon in open water and clear the surrounding area of Cnidaria and Megalodons. Approach the Archelon passively, as it is a non-violent creature and will not attack you on sight.
Swim directly up to the Archelon with Bio Toxin placed in the last slot of your hotbar. Press the interaction key (E) to feed it Bio Toxin passively to initiate the taming process.

Feeding the Archelon will cause it to generate a scent trail that spawns or aggros nearby Cnidaria (Jellyfish). Protect the Archelon from these incoming threats, as damage taken will ruin your taming effectiveness.
Track the Archelon as it swims, waiting out the feeding cooldown between bites. Continue feeding it Bio Toxin from your hotbar until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Longneck Rifle with Shocking Tranquilizer Darts or Crossbow with Tranquilizer Arrows. Bring a high-damage weapon (Shotgun or Pump-Action) to clear out surrounding herd members.; Large stack of Narcotics or Bio Toxin to prevent rapid torpor drain, and a Bear Trap or Chain Bola to immobilize the target.

steps.text: Locate your target Bison within its herd and use a high-damage weapon to eliminate the surrounding herd members. Aggroing one Bison will cause the entire group to swarm and charge you, so clearing the pack first prevents you from being overwhelmed or dismounted.

Trap the remaining target using a Bear Trap, Chain Bola, or billboard enclosure to freeze its movement. Ensure you stay at a safe distance, as its aggressive bucking and charge attacks hit extremely hard and will dismount you from standard tames.

Fire Shocking Tranquilizer Darts or Tranq Arrows into the head to build up torpor quickly. Maintain steady rhythm and pace on your shots to maximize tranquilizer effectiveness while keeping an eye on your surroundings for wandering predators.

Once the Bison drops unconscious, immediately open its inventory and load it with Narcotics/Bio Toxin alongside Superior Kibble or Crops. Monitor its torpor bar constantly, as the Bison’s torpor drains extraordinarily fast, and force-feed Narcotics to keep it asleep until the taming bar finishes.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Crossbow, Longneck Rifle, or Tek Bow loaded with Tranq Darts, Shocking Tranq Darts, or Tranq Arrows.; Ceratosaurus Venom (collected by harvesting untamed Ceratosaurus corpses), Hemomorphic Blood Cocktail (crafted in an Industrial Cooker using Ceratosaurus Venom, Blood Packs, and Cooked Meat). Place the Blood Cocktail in the last slot of your hotbar.

steps.text: Find a high-level wild Ceratosaurus and draw its aggression while riding a tanky, high-health taming mount (e.g., Stegosaurus or Megatherium). Ensure your mount is actively drinking a Hemomorphic Blood Cocktail before taking heavy hits.

Allow the Ceratosaurus to continuously attack your mount while the Blood Cocktail effect is active. Each strike forces the wild Ceratosaurus to absorb the intoxicated blood, progressively filling a hidden "Drunken" meter above its head.

Watch for the Ceratosaurus to stop attacking, stumble, and begin visually staggering in a confused, drunken state. Its aggression towards you will momentarily break, signaling that it is susceptible to torpor damage without its natural damage resistance.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Crossbow, Longneck Rifle, or Tek Bow.; Large quantities of Narcotic or Bio Toxin to maintain torpor, or cryogenic gear to withstand freezing damage.

steps.text: Target the wild Cryolophosaurus with standard tranquilizer darts, tranq arrows, or Tek Bow torpor shots from a safe distance or elevated position.

Watch for the Cryolophosaurus charging its mouth with blue cryogenic frost to unleash its freezing breath cone. Dodge horizontally out of the frost line or break line of sight to avoid getting completely frozen solid and stunned while maintaining continuous tranq pressure.

Avoid taking direct frost hits or getting trapped in close quarters, as receiving damage while chilled will stack slowness and leave you vulnerable to its high-damage bite attacks. Keep firing tranquilizers between its breath attacks to prevent its torpor from dropping.

Continue applying torpor until the Cryolophosaurus collapses into an unconscious state. Access its inventory immediately, transfer your Exceptional Kibble or high-tier meats inside, and feed Narcotics as needed to hold its torpor until the tame completes.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: High-damage Fabricated Sniper Rifle, Assault Rifle, Pump-Action Shotgun, or a strong combat tame capable of repeatedly killing the Dreadmare.; Dark Altar obtained from the Dreadmare’s corpse, plus a stockpile of land-creature tribute items such as Sarcosuchus Skin, Spinosaurus Sail, Giganotosaurus Heart, Alpha Raptor Claw, and other boss/Alpha trophies. The altar may randomly request different tributes throughout the tame.

inputs.label: None. The Dreadmare is tamed through Dark Altar sacrifices and repeated combat kills rather than conventional food

phases.name: Kill the Dreadmare and Claim Its Altar

steps.text: Fight and kill the wild Dreadmare, then collect the Dark Altar from its corpse. Place the altar before it expires; the taming ritual can only be performed at night.
Activate the Dark Altar and check which tribute it demands. Supply the requested item within 5 minutes and the altar will summon the Dreadmare back for another fight.

Immediately defeat the resurrected Dreadmare before it despawns, then return to the altar for its next tribute request. If you fail to provide the requested tribute, the altar summons both the Dreadmare **and the creature associated with that tribute** and damages itself; four failed sacrifices destroy the altar and end the tame.

phases.name: Complete the Ritual and Claim the Tame

steps.text: Repeat the tribute-and-kill cycle until the altar indicates the taming process is complete; higher-level Dreadmares can require more fights. Interact with the completed Dark Altar to destroy it and summon your fully tamed Dreadmare, with bonus levels determined by taming effectiveness.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: High-quality Crossbow or Longneck Rifle loaded with Tranquilizer Darts/Arrows.; Large Bear Traps (optional for positioning) or Ghillie Suit (if attempting to minimize ambient aggro).

steps.text: Spot the Deinosuchus in swamps or waterways and clear the immediate area of dangerous wild predators like Kaprosuchus and Titanoboa.

Wait for the Deinosuchus to pull itself onto land and enter its distinct "basking" state, opening its massive jaws wide to regulate temperature. Approach it carefully from behind or directly toward its wide-open mouth.

Move directly into its open jaws during the basking animation and press the interaction key (E) to feed it Superior Kibble or Prime Meat from your last hotbar slot. You must feed it before the basking animation completes, as the mouth will snap shut and trigger immediate aggro.

Instantly retreat back out of tail-swipe range after feeding, as the Deinosuchus will snap its jaws shut and become temporarily hostile or mobile. Repeat this passive-feeding cycle each time it enters its basking stance until the taming bar hits 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: High-damage Assault Rifle, Pump-Action Shotgun, or Fabricated Sniper Rifle.; Beer Jar (essential for the passive feeding mechanic). Place these in the last slot of your hotbar (0 key on PC).

steps.text: Approach the wild Deinotherium and shoot it with a high-damage firearm to generate maximum threat. Keep dealing damage until the Deinotherium rises onto its hind legs and enters its defensive bipedal stance.

As soon as it rears up into its bipedal stance, bait its massive downward stomp attack and quickly dodge out of the hit zone. If the stomp misses, the impact causes the creature to stagger and become briefly stunned.

Rush directly underneath the stunned Deinotherium and press the interaction key (E) to feed it a Beer Jar from your last hotbar slot. Successfully feeding it Beer will instantly drop its hostility and apply a drunken status effect.

Repeat the damage-bait-feed process until the Deinotherium collapses into a drunken unconscious state. Once it is down, open its inventory and insert Exceptional Kibble or high-tier meat to complete the tame.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: A powerful ridden combat tame for killing Corrupted creatures quickly; a Carcharodontosaurus is one of the best options. Bring a strong ranged weapon as backup.; Element placed in your last hotbar slot to initiate the passive interaction. A Cryopod containing your combat tame is highly recommended so you can deploy it once the defense phase begins.

inputs.label: Element is used to gain its attention
but the actual tame progresses by allowing the Dreadnoughtus to consume an active Element Vein. Alpha-difficulty veins provide the best taming effectiveness

steps.text: Approach without a large tame nearby and passive-feed the Dreadnoughtus Element from your hotbar. It will begin following you for roughly 60 seconds; lead it directly to an Element Vein and repeat the Element feed if you need more following time.

Once the Dreadnoughtus reaches the vein, it will approach the node, roar, and begin consuming Element. This starts the tame and removes its normal hostility toward your large combat tame, so deploy or bring in your heavy hitter immediately.

Kill every Corrupted creature that attacks the Dreadnoughtus across five waves. Each wave can provide up to 20% taming progress; every bite from the vein refreshes its protective digestion shield, but being actively attacked stops it from eating, and damage that gets through reduces taming effectiveness.

Keep the Corrupted creatures off the Dreadnoughtus until it consumes enough Element during the fifth wave to reach 100% taming progress. The remaining event attackers will die or despawn when the tame completes, and the Dreadnoughtus will immediately become yours.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Grenades or C4; explosives are required to force the buried Fasolasuchus out of the sand and begin the taming sequence.; Extra explosives for failed attempts, plus Narcotics or Bio Toxin for torpor maintenance after knockout if needed. No Tranq Arrows or Darts are required for the knockout mechanic.

phases.name: Blast It Out of the Sand

steps.text: Wait until the Fasolasuchus fully buries itself and appears as a mound of sand. Throw a Grenade onto the mound or detonate C4 over it; the explosion forces it above ground in a disoriented state, giving you a short window to run up and mount it.

Once mounted, steer the Fasolasuchus directly into breakable rock resources. Each successful collision restores your Control meter and adds torpor; Metal and Crystal nodes inflict the most torpor, with Salt also outperforming ordinary stone.

Do not let the Control meter reach zero or you will be thrown off, and avoid cliffs because sending the Fasolasuchus airborne can immediately dismount you. After each collision it briefly becomes uncontrollable and turns on its own, so regain your heading before lining up the next impact.

Continue smashing into rock, Salt, Metal, or Crystal nodes until the accumulated torpor finally knocks the Fasolasuchus unconscious. Access its inventory and load it with Exceptional Kibble, Raw Mutton, or Raw Prime Meat, using Narcotics or Bio Toxin if necessary to keep it asleep until the tame completes.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Pump-Action Shotgun, Fabricated Crossbow, or Longneck Rifle for controlled health damage; Bola can now immobilize the Pyromane while you weaken it.; Extinguisher Grenades or access to water to apply the **Doused** debuff. No Narcotics are required; this is a ride-to-tame mechanic, not a knockout tame.

inputs.label: None. Taming progress comes from setting nearby creatures on fire while mounted and using **Flame Absorb** on those flames

steps.text: Force the wild Pyromane into water or hit it with an Extinguisher Grenade to apply **Doused**, then damage it until its health falls below 50%. Once sufficiently weakened while doused, an interaction prompt appears allowing you to mount it.

phases.name: Burn Creatures and Absorb Their Flames

steps.text: While riding the wild Pyromane, attack nearby creatures to apply its burning effect. Use **Flame Absorb** on burning targets—or absorb the flames after killing them—to increase the taming meter.

Do not let too much time pass between flame absorptions; you have roughly 30 seconds to absorb more fire and continue the sequence. If the timer expires, the Pyromane throws you off, forces a cooldown before another attempt, and can reset your taming progress while reducing effectiveness.

Continue igniting creatures and absorbing their flames until the taming meter reaches 100%. The Pyromane immediately becomes yours—there is no knockout, inventory feeding, or final food interaction required.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None. Gigantoraptor is tamed through its baby; damaging or killing the adult or baby can ruin the tame.; Ghillie Armor and multiple Fertilized Eggs to distract the adult. Larger eggs are preferred because they keep the parent occupied longer while it attempts to hatch them.

inputs.label: None. The baby does not consume food during taming; Fertilized Eggs are used only to distract the adult Gigantoraptor

steps.text: Drop a Fertilized Egg away from the nest without aggroing the adult. Once the parent walks over and begins cracking the egg open, immediately move toward the nest while it is occupied.

Enter the nest and press the interaction key (E) to **Hide in Gigantoraptor Nest**. When the baby approaches and performs an action, copy it within roughly two seconds: **A to Spin, S to Bow, or D to Flap**; each correct response increases taming progress.

Do not guess the baby's action—missing the timer causes a small effectiveness loss, while performing the wrong action causes a much larger loss. When the parent finishes destroying the egg, leave the nest and distract it with another Fertilized Egg; getting aggro from the adult can reset the taming attempt.

Repeat the egg-distraction and mimic cycles until the baby's taming bar reaches 100%. Keep both the adult and baby alive throughout the process; once the final successful interaction completes the tame, the baby Gigantoraptor becomes yours without knockout feeding or narcotics.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Longneck Rifle with Shocking Tranquilizer Darts or Tranquilizer Darts; Crossbow with Tranq Arrows works as a cheaper alternative.; Narcotics or Bio Toxin for torpor maintenance if needed. Bring extra tranquilizers because shots into the armored shell deal heavily reduced damage and torpor.

inputs.label: Superior Kibble (preferred) or Raw Mutton / Raw Prime Meat / Raw Meat

steps.text: Begin firing tranquilizers into the Grand Tortugar's head or soft underbelly. Avoid the armored upper shell, which significantly reduces incoming damage and makes your tranquilizers much less effective.
Maintain steady shots into the head or belly as the Tortugar advances on you. It is a standard knockout tame, so continue building torpor until it collapses unconscious.

phases.name: Avoid the Shell and Tail Whip

steps.text: Do not waste ammunition shooting the top of its shell, and stay alert for its powerful tail attack, which can knock you away and disrupt your firing position. If fighting it in water, a Harpoon Launcher with Tranq Spear Bolts can also apply torpor effectively.

Once the Grand Tortugar falls unconscious, access its inventory and load it with Superior Kibble or meat. Use Narcotics or Bio Toxin if its torpor drops too far, then allow it to eat until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None required; the Helicoprion uses a unique passive/riding tame rather than torpor.; Bring several pieces of **looted quality equipment** from supply drops, crates, OSDs, or Gachas; crafted equipment will not work. Place **Little Ratfish Treats** in your hotbar for the feeding prompts.

steps.text: Drop a piece of eligible looted equipment directly near the Helicoprion and let it consume the item. Once it eats the equipment, immediately approach and mount it to begin the taming minigame.

Stay mounted while the Helicoprion thrashes and swims unpredictably, then press the displayed button each time a prompt appears. Complete **10 prompts**, with the final prompt using the dismount command to simultaneously feed it a Little Ratfish Treat.

Pressing the wrong button or failing to respond will throw you off and make the Helicoprion hostile. Its tail attacks can inflict heavy torpor, and its violent thrashing during the minigame can deal massive damage to nearby creatures.

After successfully feeding the Little Ratfish Treat, wait roughly **20 seconds**, drop another piece of looted equipment, and mount again. Repeat the loot-feed, riding-minigame, and Ratfish Treat cycle until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Longneck Rifle with Tranq Darts or Shocking Tranq Darts (preferred), or Crossbow with Tranq Arrows; a high-quality Longneck can potentially knock it out in a single shot.; Narcotics or Bio Toxin for torpor maintenance if needed; Maeguana has very low torpor, so only a small amount is typically required after knockout.

steps.text: Approach the Maeguana and fire as soon as you have a clean shot. Its torpor is extremely low, so a powerful Longneck with Shocking Tranq Darts can potentially drop even a high-level Maeguana in one hit.

phases.name: Stop the Glide Before It Escapes

steps.text: If the first shot does not knock it out, the Maeguana will panic, jump into the air, and glide away at very high speed. Keep landing tranquilizer shots whenever it touches down or gives you another clear firing angle.

Maeguana is skittish rather than aggressive, so its main defense is simply escaping. If it glides too far away, moving far enough to de-render it can reset its panicked state while preserving much of the torpor already inflicted, giving you another clean approach.

Continue landing tranqs until the Maeguana collapses unconscious. Access its inventory and load it with Basic Kibble, Raw Mutton, or Raw Prime Meat, using Narcotics or Bio Toxin if necessary to keep it asleep until the tame completes.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Torch only; the Megaraptor’s special taming sequence disables conventional tranquilizer tactics. Bring several Torches if using primitive-quality ones.; Durable armor and Medical Brews are strongly recommended to survive failed attack windows. You must interact with a Megaraptor Altar to begin the taming sequence.

steps.text: Find the Megaraptor’s nearby corpse altar, equip a Torch, and interact with the altar while the Megaraptor is in the area. This locks you into a small zone, heavily obscures your vision, and forces the Megaraptor into its stalking camouflage sequence.

Watch closely as the camouflaged Megaraptor approaches and prepares to strike. Swing your Torch into it **before its attack connects**; a successful interruption adds torpor and fills the special knockout bar.

Do not spam the Torch—the taming sequence increases the delay between swings, so mistiming one can leave you defenseless when the Megaraptor lunges. If you need to escape other creatures or recover, interact with the altar again to exit, but you must wait through a cooldown before restarting.

Repeat the camouflage-and-Torch counter until the special torpor bar fills and the Megaraptor falls unconscious. Access its inventory and load it with Exceptional Kibble, Raw Mutton, or meat to complete the normal knockout-feeding phase.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Sickle for removing the Shastasaurus’s attached leeches; no tranquilizer weapons are used.; At least 1 tamed Ichthyosaurus, preferably 3 to extend the leech-removal timer. SCUBA gear is highly recommended for staying mobile underwater throughout the repeated interaction cycle.

inputs.label: followed by Raw Prime Fish Meat
then Raw Fish Meat. Place your chosen food in the very last slot of your hotbar

phases.name: Get Its Attention with an Ichthy

steps.text: Ride a tamed Ichthyosaurus directly in front of the wild Shastasaurus until it becomes interested and begins following. Lead it upward to the water’s surface; once it arrives and starts socializing with your Ichthy, the taming interaction begins.

Three marked leeches will appear attached to the Shastasaurus. Swim alongside it and strike each leech with your Sickle to remove all three before the timer expires; additional nearby tamed Ichthyosaurs extend the available time, up to roughly 90 seconds with three.

Aim your Sickle carefully at the leeches—accidentally striking the Shastasaurus can disrupt the tame, while failing to remove all three within the interaction window costs taming effectiveness. Keep your Ichthyosaurs nearby so the Shasta remains interested and can quickly begin another cycle.

phases.name: Feed and Repeat the Social Cycle

steps.text: After all three leeches are removed, swim to the Shastasaurus’s mouth and press the interaction key (E) to feed Extraordinary Kibble or fish meat from your last hotbar slot. It will wander briefly afterward; let it socialize with your Ichthy again, remove another set of leeches, feed it, and repeat until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Standard Torch (un-skinned), and a high-damage weapon (e.g., Pump-Action Shotgun) for fast combat kills.; Pickaxe or Hatchet, crafting resources (such as Fiber or Stone for bulk crafting), and a timer tracking tool. Place your taming food in the very last slot of your hotbar.

inputs.label: Exceptional Kibble (preferred) or Raw Mutton / Raw Prime Meat

steps.text: Equip and light a basic, un-skinned Torch while standing near the wild Autumn Drakeling. The creature will fly down and land directly on your shoulder to initiate the passive tame.

Once perched, the Drakeling will display a prompt demanding a specific category of experience: Harvesting, Crafting, or Killing. Instantly execute actions matching that category—such as chopping trees, mass-crafting items like cloth armor or Mortar & Pestles, or slaying wild dinos—to fill its required XP progress bar.

Beware of missing the activity timer or failing to gain enough specific XP, which causes the Drakeling to jump off your shoulder and drop taming effectiveness. If given a difficult request, throw the Drakeling off into a enclosed structure to force it to reroll a new task prompt.

When the activity XP bar reaches 100%, approach the prompt and feed the Drakeling from your last hotbar slot. Repeat the task-and-feed cycles until the taming meter reaches 100% and the tame is finalized.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Standard Torch to attract the Drakeling; high-damage weapon for Kill tasks and a Pick/Hatchet for Harvest tasks. Do not use tranquilizers.; Keep a regular Torch equipped and carry lightweight crafting materials for Craft tasks. Place your taming food in the very last slot of your hotbar.

steps.text: Approach the Spring Drakeling on foot while holding a standard Torch. Once close enough, it will fly to your shoulder and begin its special passive-taming sequence.

Watch for the Drakeling to request **Harvest, Craft, or Kill** experience. Perform the requested activity until its task bar reaches 100%; higher-XP actions fill the bar faster than low-value actions.

Do not mount a creature while completing the task, as mounting suspends or interrupts the Drakeling's taming process. Keep the Drakeling on your shoulder and focus specifically on the requested XP type until the feeding prompt becomes available.

Once the task bar is full, feed the Drakeling Exceptional Kibble or meat from the last slot of your hotbar. It will then assign another Harvest, Craft, or Kill task; repeat the task-and-feed cycle until the taming bar reaches 100% and the Spring Drakeling becomes yours.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: High-damage weapon for Kill requests, plus a Pick or Hatchet for Harvest requests.; **Torch** to attract the Summer Drakeling, plus materials for quickly completing Craft requests. Place your taming food in the **last slot of your hotbar**.

steps.text: Approach the Summer Drakeling **on foot while holding a Torch**. It will be attracted to the flame, fly over, and land on your shoulder to begin the passive-taming sequence.

Watch for the Drakeling to request **Harvest, Craft, or Kill XP**, then perform that activity until its request bar fills. Higher-XP actions fill the bar faster, so harvest valuable resources, craft worthwhile items, or kill creatures efficiently.

phases.name: Stay on Foot and Follow the Prompt

steps.text: Do not mount another creature during the process; mounting suspends the tame and interferes with the Drakeling's shoulder interaction. Complete only the currently displayed XP category, then be ready to feed as soon as its bar reaches 100%.

Once the requested XP bar is full, press the interaction key (E) to feed **Exceptional Kibble** from your last hotbar slot. The Summer Drakeling will then choose another Harvest, Craft, or Kill request; repeat the task-and-feed cycle until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Combat weapon or strong tame for completing **Kill** objectives; no tranquilizers are required because the Winter Drakeling is a passive tame.; Torch to attract the Drakeling, plus materials/tools for completing **Craft**, **Harvest**, or **Kill** XP objectives. Keep your chosen taming food in the very last slot of your hotbar.

inputs.label: Exceptional Kibble (preferred) or Cooked Prime Meat

steps.text: Approach the wild Winter Drakeling on foot while holding a lit Torch. Once attracted, it will fly down and perch on your shoulder, beginning the passive taming sequence.

While perched, the Drakeling will randomly request **Harvest**, **Craft**, or **Kill**. Perform that activity to earn XP toward its objective bar—higher-value actions, such as crafting more expensive structures, fill the bar faster than cheap actions.

phases.name: Stay on Foot and Follow the Prompt

steps.text: Do not mount a creature while working on the objective; mounting suspends the Drakeling's taming process. Complete only the requested XP category until its bar fills, then prepare the food in your last hotbar slot.

Once the objective bar is full, feed the Winter Drakeling Exceptional Kibble or Cooked Prime Meat from your last hotbar slot. It will then assign another random Harvest, Craft, or Kill objective; repeat the complete-and-feed cycle until the taming bar reaches 100% and the Winter Drakeling becomes yours.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Crossbow with Tranq Arrows (preferred underwater) or Harpoon Launcher with Tranq Spear Bolts.; Narcotics or Bio Toxin; Xiphactinus torpor drains quickly once unconscious, so keep a healthy supply ready.

steps.text: Aggro the Xiphactinus and repeatedly hit it with Tranq Arrows or Tranq Spear Bolts while maintaining distance. Keep steady pressure until its torpor climbs toward the knockout threshold.
Once its torpor gets high, stay on the fleeing Xiphactinus and continue landing controlled tranquilizer shots. Stop firing immediately when it collapses so you do not add unnecessary damage.

Do not fight from a small or fragile aquatic mount—the Xiphactinus can grab smaller creatures, violently thrash them, and inflict heavy bleeding damage. Keep yourself and vulnerable mounts out of its jaws while applying torpor.

Access the unconscious Xiphactinus immediately and load it with Superior Kibble, Raw Mutton, or Raw Prime Meat. Closely monitor its rapidly dropping torpor and force-feed Narcotics or Bio Toxin as needed until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: No tranquilizer weapons; Tranq Arrows and Tranq Darts do not build torpor on a wild Yi Ling. A Shield is useful for blocking its ground attacks while waiting for the taming sequence.; Plant Species Z Fruit to stun it during its dive attack, plus Bio Toxin (preferred, 300 torpor per feed) or Narcotics. Place the Bio Toxin or Narcotics in the very last slot of your hotbar.

steps.text: Let the wild Yi Ling remain airborne and repeatedly hit you with its ranged feather attack. Once you accumulate at least 30 feather stacks, watch its wings—a faint red glow while gliding signals that it is preparing to dive-bomb you.

As the Yi Ling commits to its dive, throw a Plant Species Z Fruit directly at it. If timed correctly, the explosion interrupts the dive and temporarily stuns the Yi Ling; immediately run up and feed it Bio Toxin or Narcotics from your last hotbar slot to raise its torpor.

phases.name: Do Not Waste the Stun Window

steps.text: Plant Species Z Fruit only works for taming while the Yi Ling is performing its dive animation, so throwing it too early or too late accomplishes nothing. If it lands and begins biting instead, avoid or block it until it takes flight again, rebuild/maintain the required feather stacks, and wait for another red-glowing dive.

Repeat the feather-stack, dive-stun, and narcotic-feed cycle until the Yi Ling finally falls unconscious. Once asleep, access its inventory and load it with Exceptional Kibble, Raw Mutton, or Raw Prime Meat to finish the tame.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Drake Claw to initiate the tame; strong ranged weaponry for the airborne combat phase against spawned Argentavis and Pteranodons.; Drake Claw is mandatory to interact with and mount the landed Umbra. No tranquilizers, Narcotics, or torpor-maintenance items are required.

inputs.label: Extraordinary Kibble (preferred) or Cooked Lamb Chop

steps.text: Wait for the Umbra to land, approach it, and use the Drake Claw to begin the interaction; activation takes roughly 5 seconds. Once successful, the Umbra takes off with you and starts its multi-phase taming challenge.

During the mimic phase, watch the Umbra perform Barrel Rolls, Backflips, and Quick Turns, then repeat the same inputs in sequence. A new maneuver appears roughly every 5 seconds, and you have about 30 seconds to complete the pattern correctly.

Kill the spawned Argentavis and Pteranodons **without taking damage**, because getting hit reduces your progress; afterward, complete the required travel-distance phase before its timer expires. Keep moving at maximum speed and use steep dives for faster travel progress.

After completing all three challenges, the Umbra calms down and gives you roughly 20 seconds to feed it Extraordinary Kibble or Cooked Lamb Chop. The entire mimic → combat → travel → feed cycle then restarts; repeat it until the taming bar reaches 100% and the Umbra becomes yours.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Tek Quetzal platform with Tek Turrets, Crossbow with Grappling Hooks, or high-damage Wyverns / Lightning Wyverns.; Parachutes, Glider Suit, or Grappling Hooks to clear corrupted nodes and land safely.

inputs.label: None (Static mechanical tame upon defeating node corruption)

steps.text: Spawn the Desert Titan at the Desert Cave terminal, then mount a flying creature or use grappling mechanics to position yourself near the three distinct Corrupted Nodes on its body (tail, right wing, left wing).
Attack the corrupted node located on the tail until it bursts; destroying this node forces the Titan to spawn Flock swarms and trigger localized lightning strikes.

Maneuver yourself or your tame directly over the corrupted nodes on each wing to bait the Titan's lightning strikes into hitting its own nodes, damaging them without destroying the Titan's main health bar.

Once all three corrupted nodes are successfully destroyed, the Desert Titan will fall to the ground and temporarily pass out; land on its back, access its platform saddle area, and press the interaction key to instantly claim it.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Fabricated Sniper Rifle or Assault Rifle with plenty of ammunition; a Mek with its Mek Pistol is also highly effective for safely targeting the corruption nodes.; No narcotics or special taming items are required. Bring enough ammunition or Element to destroy all three corruption nodes while minimizing accidental body damage.

inputs.label: None. The Forest Titan does not eat taming food; it is claimed by interacting with it after removing all corruption

steps.text: Target the large corrupted node on one shoulder and repeatedly shoot it until it breaks, then repeat the process on the opposite shoulder. Successful hits make the corruption visibly react; concentrate every shot on the node rather than the Titan's body.

Once both shoulder nodes are destroyed, the final corruption node will appear underneath the Forest Titan's chin. Reposition until you have a clear angle and focus all fire directly into this final growth.

Minimize shots that hit the Titan itself, as unnecessary damage lowers the quality and health of the resulting tame. After losing its first corruption node, expect more dangerous attacks, including its vine grab that can pull you from a Mek and its large-area root attack.

phases.name: Break the Final Node and Claim

steps.text: Destroy the chin corruption and the Forest Titan will collapse onto the ground. Approach its downed body and press the interaction key (E) to instantly tame it; no knockout food is required, and its special Platform Saddle is automatically equipped.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None. Gacha is a passive tame and should not be damaged during the taming process.; Large quantities of droppable structures. Stacks of 20 Tek Foundations provide the highest effectiveness, followed by Metal Foundations; stacks of 20 Cooking Pots are a strong cheaper alternative.

inputs.label: Tek Foundations (best) > Metal Foundations > Cooking Pots > Stone Foundations; Snow Owl Pellets can also be consumed
but structure stacks are substantially more effective for taming

steps.text: Approach the wild Gacha and make sure it is happy before attempting to tame it. A Gacha that has recently been near other Gachas can become sad and will refuse to eat; do not damage it, as taking damage can also prevent feeding.

Stand in front of the Gacha and drop a stack of 20 structures directly onto the ground from your inventory. The Gacha will walk over, pick up the entire dropped stack, and begin eating it automatically to gain taming progress.

Continue dropping stacks where the Gacha can easily reach them, allowing it to finish eating each supply. Do not attack it or allow nearby Gachas to make it sad, or it can stop consuming your dropped items and interrupt the tame.

Repeat the drop-and-eat cycle with full structure stacks until the taming bar reaches 100%. The Gacha will automatically become yours after its final feeding; there is no knockout, inventory feeding, or manual interaction required.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Longneck Rifle with Tranquilizer Darts or Crossbow with Tranquilizer Arrows.; Narcotics or Bio Toxin for torpor maintenance if needed. Bring extra tranquilizers because Gasbags take heavily reduced damage while fully inflated.

steps.text: Shoot the Gasbags with tranquilizer darts or arrows to begin raising its torpor. It will immediately try to flee rather than fight, often inflating and launching itself away.
When it inflates, aim specifically for the head. Headshots while it is puffing up force it to deflate, removing its 80% damage reduction and helping prevent it from launching away.

Keep following and landing tranquilizer shots as it runs. Avoid wasting shots into its inflated body whenever possible, and watch for its gas blast, which can knock you away and interrupt your firing position.

Continue applying torpor until the Gasbags collapses unconscious. Access its inventory, load it with Superior Kibble or crops, and use Narcotics or Bio Toxin if its torpor begins dropping too far before the tame finishes.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Longneck Rifle with Tranquilizer Darts or Shocking Tranquilizer Darts; Crossbow with Tranq Arrows as a cheaper alternative.; Chain Bola, Large Bear Trap, or Plant Species Y can immobilize the Managarmr long enough to land repeated tranqs. Bring Narcotics or Bio Toxin for torpor maintenance if needed.

inputs.label: followed by Raw Mutton / Raw Prime Meat / Raw Meat

steps.text: Use a Chain Bola, Large Bear Trap, or Plant Species Y to stop its extreme mobility. Once restrained, immediately start firing Tranq Darts into its body.

Keep landing tranq shots while it is immobilized or whenever it lands. Managarmrs frequently jump, dash, and boost into the air, so capitalize on every stationary window before it launches away again.

phases.name: Avoid the Freeze and Boost Attacks

steps.text: Stay out of its frontal freezing breath and be ready for sudden lunges or aerial boosts that can quickly reposition it. Do not chase recklessly between shots; wait for a clean landing or another immobilization opportunity before continuing.

Once the Managarmr collapses, access its inventory and load it with Exceptional Kibble or Raw Mutton. Monitor its torpor and force-feed Narcotics or Bio Toxin if necessary until the taming meter reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Cannon with Cannon Balls; direct headshots are required to inflict meaningful torpor. A Rocket Launcher can work, but the Cannon is safer for preserving health and taming effectiveness.; Extra Cannon Balls for missed shots and Narcotics or Bio Toxin as backup torpor maintenance during slower feeding methods.

steps.text: Approach until the disguised Ice Golem rises from its resting form and becomes aggressive. Get it facing toward you so its head remains exposed for clean cannon shots.

phases.name: Hammer the Head with Cannon Balls

steps.text: Fire the Cannon directly into the Ice Golem's head. Successful headshots inflict the torpor needed for the knockout; continue landing controlled shots until its torpor climbs high enough.

Do not repeatedly hit its torso, arms, or legs—poorly placed explosive hits deal health damage without providing the necessary knockout progress and can kill the Ice Golem. Take your time between shots and make every Cannon Ball connect with the head.

Continue landing direct cannon headshots until the Ice Golem collapses unconscious. Access its inventory and load it with Extraordinary Kibble, Sulfur, Clay, or Stone, using Narcotics or Bio Toxin if necessary to keep it asleep until the tame completes.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None for taming. The Mega Mek is not knocked out or passive-tamed; it is assembled from existing Meks.; 4 deployed Meks total and 1 M.O.M.I. (MegaMek Operational Materialization Interface). Equip the M.O.M.I. into one Mek's module slot while three additional Meks are standing nearby.

inputs.label: None. The Mega Mek does not consume taming food and has no taming effectiveness process

steps.text: Place four owned Meks close together and enter the Mek that will carry the M.O.M.I. If more than three additional Meks are nearby, the three closest are selected for the fusion.

Insert the M.O.M.I. into your Mek's module slot to initiate the Mega Mek transformation. The interface requires three nearby Meks and will only function while an Alpha King Titan is present and within the required encounter range.

phases.name: Meet the Alpha King Titan Requirement

steps.text: Do not attempt the fusion outside the Alpha King Titan fight—the Mega Mek cannot be properly formed or used without that Omega-level threat active. All four Meks used in the fusion are combined into the resulting Mega Mek.

Activate the M.O.M.I. with all requirements met and the four Meks merge into a level 1500 Mega Mek under your control. No knockout, feeding, or claiming step is required; once the transformation completes, you can immediately pilot the Mega Mek against the Alpha King Titan.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Longneck Rifle with Tranquilizer Darts or Shocking Tranquilizer Darts; avoid relying on Tranq Arrows because the Snow Owl has relatively low health compared with its torpor.; Net Projectile to immobilize the Snow Owl for up to a minute, plus Narcotics or Bio Toxin as backup torpor maintenance after knockout.

steps.text: Hit the flying Snow Owl with a Net Projectile to force it down and immobilize it. Immediately switch to your Longneck Rifle and begin landing Tranq Darts while it cannot escape.
Continue firing Tranq Darts until the Snow Owl approaches its knockout threshold. A high-level Owl can require a substantial number of tranqs, so keep steady pressure while the Net holds it in place.

Snow Owls have relatively low health for the amount of torpor required, making high-damage Crossbows and rapid Tranq Arrow spam risky. Favor darts and allow the delayed torpor from your final shots to apply before firing unnecessarily again.
