Once the Snow Owl collapses unconscious, access its inventory and load it with Superior Kibble, Raw Mutton, or Raw Prime Meat. Its torpor drains slowly enough that Narcotics are often unnecessary, but monitor the bar and force-feed them if needed until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Longneck Rifle with Tranquilizer Darts or Crossbow with Tranq Arrows; ranged tranquilizers are strongly preferred because the Velonasaur can punish you heavily at distance.; Narcotics, Bio Toxin, or Narcoberries for torpor maintenance. Bring enough tranq ammunition to finish the knockout without being forced into close combat.

steps.text: Hit the Velonasaur with Tranq Darts or Tranq Arrows and immediately keep moving. Once provoked, it will aggressively pursue and use both melee attacks and ranged spine volleys.

Continue landing controlled tranquilizer shots while avoiding prolonged exposure directly in front of it. When the Velonasaur stops and enters its stationary spine-shooting stance, move sideways or use available cover until the volley ends, then resume firing.

Do not stand still and trade shots while it is firing; its rapid projectile attack can shred armor and health surprisingly fast. As its torpor rises it will eventually attempt to flee, so keep pressure on it without adding unnecessary damage.

Continue applying torpor until the Velonasaur falls unconscious, then access its inventory and load it with Regular Kibble or your best available meat. Monitor its torpor and force-feed Narcotics, Bio Toxin, or Narcoberries as needed until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Crossbow or Longneck Rifle loaded with Tranquilizer Darts/Arrows (only used to clear surrounding threats).; Giant Bee Honey. Place the honey directly into your hotbar for quick deployment.

inputs.label: Giant Bee Honey (it acts as both the taming lure and the taming feed)

steps.text: Throw a stack of Giant Bee Honey onto the ground near the Andrewsarchus from a safe distance. Wait for it to approach and start eating the honey, then quietly sneak up behind it and press the interaction key (E) to jump onto its back.

Once mounted, directional steering arrows will appear on your screen along with a rage meter. Hold the indicated directional key (Left or Right) to keep the vehicle-like steering under control, but release the key immediately before the red rage bar fills up to prevent it from bucking you off.

Keep the Andrewsarchus running in open space, avoiding walls, rocks, and wild predators. If the rage meter gets too high, dismount immediately, run to a safe distance, throw down another piece of Honey, and repeat the mounting process.
Successfully riding the creature while managing its steering and rage will steadily fill its taming meter. Once the meter hits 100%, the Andrewsarchus is fully tamed and ready for a saddle.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: High-quality Crossbow or Longneck Rifle loaded with Tranquilizer Darts, plus a Shotgun to clear surrounding threats.; Blood Packs (30–100+ depending on level), Medical Brews, and a sacrificial high-health tame (e.g., Moschops or Megaloceros) on "Passive."

inputs.label: Blood Packs (mandatory for taming progress; superior effectiveness comes from taming effectiveness mechanics)

steps.text: Wipe out all surrounding bats, spiders, and centipedes in the immediate area to ensure a safe taming environment. Place at least 50+ Blood Packs into your inventory before approaching.
Walk or fly directly under the sleeping Desmodus clinging to the ceiling. Let it swoop down, grab you in its talons, and begin actively consuming the Blood Packs from your inventory.

Allow the Desmodus to repeatedly pick up and drain blood from your sacrificial tame set to Passive. Each successful grab on your sacrificial creature rapidly charges the Desmodus's taming effectiveness multiplier up to 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Strong boss-fighting tames such as bred Rexes, Shadowmanes, or Spinos, ideally supported by a Yutyrannus; bring a high-quality Pump-Action Shotgun as backup.; Gamma, Beta, or Alpha Broodmother, Megapithecus, and Dragon Trophies matching the Fenrisúlfr difficulty you intend to summon.

inputs.label: None. Fenrir is not food-tamed; it is awarded already tamed inside a Cryopod after defeating Fenrisúlfr

steps.text: Place the matching Broodmother, Megapithecus, and Dragon trophies into an Obelisk and start the Gamma, Beta, or Alpha Fenrisúlfr encounter. Gamma requires level 55, Beta 75, and Alpha 100.

Attack Fenrisúlfr aggressively with your boss army while dealing with the Fenrir minions it summons. Keep your main damage tames focused on Fenrisúlfr and use your Yutyrannus to maintain its Courage buff.

Watch for Fenrisúlfr's powerful frost abilities and attacks that can immobilize or heavily damage your creatures. Do not mistake the summoned Fenrir minions for tameable targets—they cannot be claimed or normally tamed during the fight.

Kill Fenrisúlfr to receive a Fenrir already contained inside a Cryopod—no knockout or feeding phase is required. The reward is level 150 from Gamma, 190 from Beta, or 225 from Alpha; normally, the survivor who initiated the boss fight receives the Fenrir Cryopod.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None. Do not use tranquilizers—the Rare X-Sabertooth Salmon is torpor-immune and is captured rather than knocked out.; Fish Basket. Place it underwater near the Rare X-Sabertooth Salmon and wait for the basket to become ready for capture.

inputs.label: None. Rare X-Sabertooth Salmon are tamed directly through the Fish Basket mechanic

steps.text: Set a Fish Basket underwater close to the Rare X-Sabertooth Salmon you want. Let the fish swim within the basket's capture range rather than attacking or attempting to build torpor.

Stay near the basket and watch for the capture interaction to become available while the Salmon is close enough. Press the interaction key (E) to capture it, converting the basket into a Filled Fish Basket.

Do not attack the target while positioning it; injured Sabertooth Salmon can turn aggressive and cause nearby Salmon to swarm you. Their bites can also apply a stamina-draining bleed, making underwater escape harder.

Deploy the Filled Fish Basket back into water to release the Rare X-Sabertooth Salmon as your tame. No knockout, Narcotics, food, or additional taming phase is required; never release it on land, as the fish will immediately die.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Harpoon Gun with Net Projectiles (for easy immobilization) or a Crossbow/Tek Rifle (for clearing surrounding hostiles).; Parachutes, Grappling Hooks, and Medical Brews.

inputs.label: Blood Packs (requires ~100–1,500 depending on creature level and server multipliers)

steps.text: Locate the Bloodstalker on tree trunks or ceiling arches in the Bog/Redwood biomes, clear all surrounding wild dinos below it, and maneuver directly underneath its position.
Allow the Bloodstalker to target you with its web-string reel attack; do not attack or resist as it pulls you up toward its mouth.

Keep Blood Packs in your main inventory so it passively drains them to gain taming progress upon reaching its mouth. If your health drops below 40%, consume Medical Brews to avoid dying before the process completes.

To reach maximum taming efficiency, feed it tamed sacrificial creatures (like Sacrificed Moss Chops or Megaloceros) by letting the Bloodstalker grab them before it grabs you. Once full efficiency is gained, let it grab you to finish feeding Blood Packs until tamed.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None required for taming; the Ferox is a passive tame. Bring strong armor or a fast mount only to survive its transformed aggressive form.; Place **Element** in your hotbar and keep enough for repeated transformations. The amount required increases with the Ferox's level, reaching roughly 20 transformations for a level 150.

inputs.label: **Element only**; Ferox does not use kibble

steps.text: Approach the Ferox while it is in its small form and use Element from your hotbar while looking directly at it. Feeding the Element starts taming and immediately triggers its transformation into the large form.
As soon as it transforms, get away from it. The giant Ferox becomes highly aggressive, will chase and attack you, and cannot receive the next taming feed until it reverts to its small form.

phases.name: Do Not Feed the Wrong Form

steps.text: Wait out the entire transformation instead of trying to approach the giant Ferox. Each Element feed also increases its Addiction meter, making the transformed creature stronger while shortening how long the transformation lasts.

Once it shrinks back into its small form, approach and feed another Element to trigger the next cycle. Repeat the feed-transform-survive-revert sequence until the final transformation ends and the Ferox becomes tamed.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: High-quality Tek Rifle, Harpoon Launcher with Translocator/Net Projectiles (if applicable), or a heavy-damage ranged weapon.; Element (required to power Tek Rifle or Tek gear used to chip health/torpor).

steps.text: Locate the Astrocetus floating in the Lunar biome or Space zone and clear nearby void threats like Seekers or Drone units. Draw its attention from a safe distance using a Tek Rifle or fast hover mount to keep it focused on you.

Aim exclusively for the whale's head, as body shots do not deal optimal torpor damage. Fire your Tek Rifle continuously at its skull to build up its torpor meter while maintaining a safe distance from its massive tail sweeps.

Watch for the Astrocetus to charge up its hyperspace warp or cosmic tail swipes, which can easily throw you out of position or destroy your gear. Circle strafe constantly while firing to stay clear of its frontal cone attack zone.

Once the Astrocetus reaches max torpor, it will pass out and drift in zero gravity. Instantly fly up to its inventory, insert Exceptional Kibble or Raw Mutton, and defend the floating body from wild predators until the tame completes.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None required for the actual tame; optionally bring a Longneck Rifle with Tranquilizer Darts to knock the Noglin out and reset its behavior if it repeatedly refuses to mind-control your creatures.; Bring multiple full-health tamed creatures and set them to **Passive**. For maximum taming effectiveness, use no more than 5 high-level Brontosaurus or Voidwyrms; Cryopods are useful for rotating already-controlled creatures out.

inputs.label: Live tamed creatures—the Noglin gains taming progress by completing mind-control sessions on them. Brontosaurus / Voidwyrm are preferred for maximum effectiveness; Carbonemys are a safer

steps.text: Place a full-health tame near the wild Noglin with the creature set to Passive. Stay back and allow the Noglin to leap onto its head and begin a full mind-control session; completing the possession adds taming progress.

Once the Noglin releases a creature, move or Cryopod that tame and present a fresh one. Wild Noglins strongly resist possessing the same creature twice during one taming attempt, so cycling different hosts keeps the tame progressing.

phases.name: Protect the Noglin from Its Victims

steps.text: Keep every offered creature on Passive—the possessed tame can attack nearby targets, and your own creatures can easily kill the fragile Noglin if they retaliate. Mind control also drains the host's health, so start each offering healthy and avoid using excessively dangerous damage dealers.

Continue offering fresh tames until a completed mind-control session pushes the taming meter to 100%. For maximum effectiveness, complete the tame within 5 hosts—Brontosaurus and Voidwyrms can provide enough affinity to accomplish this without exceeding the five-creature limit.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None. Shadowmane is a passive tame and should not be damaged during the taming process.; Full Ghillie Armor, Bug Repellant, and multiple Filled Fish Baskets. Place a Filled Fish Basket containing a fish weighing **over 0.5** in the very last slot of your hotbar; larger fish provide substantially more taming progress.

inputs.label: Filled Fish Baskets containing large Coelacanth
Sabertooth Salmon; larger/heavier fish are preferred

steps.text: Shadowmanes rest during the daytime. Stay outside its detection range until your target lies down and falls asleep, then crouch toward it while wearing Ghillie Armor.

Approach strictly from the Shadowmane's rear or side while it sleeps. With the Filled Fish Basket in your last hotbar slot, press the interaction key (E) when the feeding prompt appears; after eating, it will wake, turn invisible, and move to another location.

Never approach from the front, attack it, or disturb nearby sleeping Shadowmanes—the entire pack can wake and aggro, and waking your target through your actions can reset its taming progress. After every feeding, back away, track the Shadowmane's new position, and wait for it to fall asleep again before approaching.

Each time the Shadowmane falls asleep, sneak behind it and feed another Filled Fish Basket. Continue using the largest fish possible until the taming bar reaches 100%; it will automatically become yours after the final successful feeding with no knockout or Narcotics required.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Longneck Rifle with Tranquilizer Darts or Crossbow with Tranq Arrows.; Narcotics or Bio Toxin for torpor maintenance if needed; Maewing has relatively low torpor and can wake quickly.

inputs.label: followed by Crops / Mejoberries / other Berries

steps.text: Shoot the Maewing with Tranq Darts or Tranq Arrows until its torpor starts climbing. Aim carefully and avoid excessive damage because Maewings have relatively low health compared with larger knockout tames.
Once frightened, the Maewing will rapidly glide, jump, and slide away from you. Keep pressure on it whenever it lands and continue applying torpor before it can create too much distance.

phases.name: Do Not Lose Sight of It

steps.text: Maewings can cover a huge amount of ground in seconds and may glide over terrain or into dangerous areas. Avoid long pauses between shots so its torpor does not drain while you are chasing it.
Once the Maewing falls unconscious, access its inventory and load it with Basic Kibble or berries. Use Narcotics or Bio Toxin if necessary to keep it asleep until the taming meter reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Harpoon Gun loaded with Net Projectiles (optional, to lock down movements) or a standard Crossbow/Longneck for defensive clear.; Element (required for passive taming). Place the Element directly into the last slot of your hotbar.

steps.text: Fly up to the Astrodelphis on a flying mount or Tek Suit and dismount nearby to approach it in zero gravity. Walk up to the wild Astrodelphis and press the interaction key (E) to "Pet" it, which initiates the taming process and grants a temporary taming effectiveness buff.

Immediately after petting it, press the interaction key (E) a second time to feed it Element from your last hotbar slot. You must feed it a second piece of Element shortly after the first to satisfy its initial hunger prompt before it flies away.

Once fed, the Astrodelphis will emit a star-burst effect and sprint away rapidly in space. Use a Tek Suit or fast flyer to keep up with it while avoiding its aggressive spin attacks and plasma blasts if it aggroes onto you.
Wait for the Astrodelphis to calm down and prompt for another pet/feed cycle. Repeat the "Pet then Feed" combo repeatedly before the taming effectiveness timer decays until the tame reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None required; the Tek Stryder is tamed through a non-violent hacking minigame and is torpor immune.; **Mutagel** placed in the **last slot of your hotbar**, plus enough completed unique Genesis: Part 2 missions to meet the Stryder's level requirement. A level 150 requires **49 completed missions**.

inputs.label: **Mutagel only**; the required amount increases with the Tek Stryder's level and is consumed during successful hacking stages

steps.text: Approach the Tek Stryder and look for the specific body part emitting electrical sparks—such as its head or one of its feet. If you have enough Mutagel and meet its mission requirement, interact with that point to begin the hack.

Stay close enough to keep the Tek Stryder inside the large red circle around you while lines of code scroll across the hacking interface. Press the input when each **green square crosses the horizontal center line**, repeating until every column is completed.

phases.name: Do Not Fail or Leave the Circle

steps.text: Missing the hacking inputs can **reset your taming progress to 0%** and briefly stun you. After each attempt, the Stryder must walk a certain distance from the previous hacking location before another hack can begin, so follow it and watch for the next sparking body part.

Repeat the approach-and-hack cycle, consuming Mutagel as required and successfully completing each minigame. Once the final hack fills the taming bar to 100%, the Tek Stryder immediately becomes yours with its built-in platform, transmitter, and permanent head/body rigs intact.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Pump-Action Shotgun (preferred), Fabricated Sniper Rifle, Tek Bow, or another controlled high-damage ranged weapon to reduce the Voidwyrm’s health without killing it.; Mutagen placed in the very last slot of your hotbar; a Net Projectile and Harpoon Launcher are highly effective for holding the Voidwyrm still while lowering its health.

steps.text: Damage the wild Voidwyrm until it reaches the required low-health threshold and becomes ready to tame. A Net Projectile can pin it down while you carefully reduce its health with a Shotgun or other ranged weapon; wait for the net to release before attempting to mount it.

Once sufficiently injured, the Voidwyrm briefly slows and shows blue thruster flames near the base of its wings. Approach from the side and interact to mount it, beginning an Equus-style riding tame while keeping Mutagen in your last hotbar slot.

Stay mounted until the Voidwyrm performs a barrel roll and the feeding prompt flashes on-screen. Immediately press the interaction key (E) to feed Mutagen; missing the short window causes it to throw you off and reduces both taming progress and effectiveness.
Remount if necessary and continue riding, feeding Mutagen every time the barrel-roll prompt appears. Repeat the ride-and-feed cycle until the taming meter reaches 100% and the Voidwyrm becomes yours.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Longneck Rifle or Fabricated Crossbow; use accurate ranged shots to eliminate nearby Revenants and specifically hit the Gloon’s eyes.; Stay crouched while approaching to avoid triggering the Gloon’s detection. No narcotics or torpor-maintenance items are required; this is a passive tame after you deflate its eyes.

inputs.label: Basic Kibble (preferred) or Plant Proto Species R Seed; Aquatic
Aggeravic Mushrooms and various meats can also be used. Place your chosen food in the last slot of your hotbar

steps.text: Crouch beneath or around the floating Gloon without entering its detection radius, then eliminate the Revenants surrounding it. Keep the Gloon itself unaggroed while clearing the group, because aggression prevents you from progressing cleanly into the passive-tame phase.

Aim exclusively at the Gloon’s large glowing eyes and shoot them with bullets or arrows. Each successful eye hit deflates it and forces the Gloon progressively lower until it is hovering near ground level and its eyes stop glowing.

Do not hit the Gloon’s body—body damage triggers aggression and can ruin the setup. If it spots you beforehand, its Mesmerize attack can force your character into uncontrolled movement while nearby Revenants attack, so stay crouched and only take precise eye shots.

Once the Gloon reaches ground level and its glowing eyes deactivate, approach and feed it Basic Kibble or Plant Proto Species R Seed from your last hotbar slot. Wait for each feeding interval and repeat the passive feeds until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: High-damage Compound Bow, Pump-Action Shotgun, or Tek Rifle for defending against wave spawns.; Requested offering gifts (Apprentice tier or higher tools, weapons, or rare resources requested by the creature) in your hotbar, plus a Parachute or Glider Suit.

inputs.label: Raw Mutton or Raw Meat (used for raising the baby post-hatch)

steps.text: Approach the neutral Aureliax in the wild and check its requested item prompt. Place the specific weapon, tool, or resource it demands into your last hotbar slot and interact with the creature to submit the gift.

Continue submitting requested offerings until the Aureliax is satisfied. Once fulfilled, the creature will transform into a massive giant egg and drop to the ground, dismounting you instantly (use a glider or parachute to land safely).

Prepare for combat as the egg emits a light beam and initiates five waves of aggressive enemy spawns. Protect the egg's health bar by drawing enemy aggro onto yourself and eliminating all hostiles in each wave.

After clearing all five enemy waves, walk directly up to the egg and press the interaction key to claim the fertilized Aureliax egg into your inventory. Take the egg back to base, incubate it using Air Conditioners, hatch the baby, and hand-feed it meat to complete the tame.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Longneck Rifle with Tranquilizer Darts (recommended) or Crossbow with Tranq Arrows; you only need to raise the Ossidon to roughly 50% torpor, not fully knock it out.; Sanguine Elixir (optional; use only after the third rolling phase for best effectiveness). No Narcotics are required because the Ossidon is never fully knocked unconscious.

inputs.label: None. Taming progress comes from rolling up **wild creatures** and catching the Ossidon’s own fired icicles while riding it; your own tamed creatures cannot be absorbed

steps.text: Shoot the wild Ossidon with Tranq Darts or Tranq Arrows until its torpor reaches roughly 50%. When stars appear over its head and it becomes dazed, immediately approach and mount it.

phases.name: Form the Bolus and Start Rolling

steps.text: While mounted, use the secondary attack to form the Ossidon’s rolling bolus. Roll through wild creatures to absorb them, then catch the icicles the Ossidon periodically fires; grabbing roughly five creatures first and then prioritizing icicles is an effective sequence.

Each new mounting cycle drops taming effectiveness by roughly 25%, but collecting the required icicles restores it toward 100%. Do not waste time trying to absorb your own tames—they were patched out of the mechanic—and keep completing the required creature/icicle objectives before the riding timer expires.

After each bolus phase ends, repeat the half-torpor daze, mount, and rolling minigame until the taming meter reaches 100%; normally this requires multiple rides. If using a Sanguine Elixir, apply it after the third completed rolling phase to accelerate the finish without sacrificing full taming effectiveness.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None; Veilwyn uses a stealth-claim taming mechanic and should not be attacked or knocked out.; No special items are required. Crouch-walking and approaching from directly behind are the key mechanics; tranquilizers, Narcotics, and passive-feed items are unnecessary.

inputs.label: None; despite listing Exceptional Kibble as its preferred food after taming
Veilwyn requires no food during the actual claim-taming process

steps.text: Crouch and slowly approach the wild Veilwyn from directly behind without entering its field of view. Stay concealed until you are close enough for the interaction prompt to appear.
When you successfully reach it unnoticed, a **“Claim Veilwyn”** prompt will appear. Immediately press the interaction key (E) to claim it; there is no feeding interval or taming bar to fill.

If the Veilwyn spots you, it will begin producing identical clones, making it extremely difficult to identify the real creature. If the group grows to roughly five or more Veilwyns, back away completely—large clone groups become aggressive and can quickly overwhelm you.

Wait for the clones to disappear if your first approach fails, then crouch-sneak behind the original again. Reach the **“Claim Veilwyn”** prompt without being detected and interact once to instantly complete the tame.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: High-quality Crossbow or Longneck Rifle loaded with Tranq Arrows or Tranq Darts.; Calien Soup or Shadow Steak Saute. Place this item in the far-right slot of your hotbar.

inputs.label: Exceptional Kibble (preferred) or Raw Mutton / Raw Prime Meat

steps.text: Eat your Calien Soup or Shadow Steak Saute before approaching the Amargasaurus to prevent it from immediately attacking you. Approach the creature passively without aggressive tames or weapons drawn.

Walk up to the Amargasaurus and press the interaction key (E) to feed it the consumable from your last hotbar slot. The Amargasaurus will enter a temporary "synced" state and follow you, matching your movements without targeting you.
Lead the Amargasaurus toward aggressive wild creatures and fight alongside it. The Amargasaurus must deal damage to or participate in killing aggressive targets to fill its taming percentage bar.
Keep the Amargasaurus alive and avoid ambient environmental extremes,

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None; Sinomacrops is a passive tame and should not be knocked unconscious.; Chitin placed in the very last slot of your hotbar. Avoid Chitin Armor, nearby tames, and anything that may spook it during the feeding cycle.

steps.text: Walk slowly near the Sinomacrops with Chitin ready and allow it to come toward you. Do not sprint or jump—sudden movement can scare it away before you get the first feed.

When the interaction prompt appears, press the interaction key (E) to feed it Chitin. It will immediately fly away for a short period; track and follow it until hearts appear and it begins returning toward you for another feed.

Stay outside with clear ground nearby so the Sinomacrops can land and approach you properly. Wearing any Chitin Armor makes it aggressive, while sprinting, jumping, nearby tames, or preventing it from landing can cause it to flee and disrupt the tame.

Each time the Sinomacrops returns with hearts and the feeding prompt reappears, give it another piece of Chitin. Repeat the feed-follow-return cycle until the taming meter reaches 100% and the Sinomacrops becomes yours.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Heavy Turrets or Mounted Minuguns (to strip armor rapidly), and a High-Damage Pump-Action Shotgun or Fabricated Sniper Rifle.; Elemental Dust or Bio Toxin. Place these items in the last slot of your hotbar for quick access.

steps.text: Open fire on the Chalk Golem with high-dps weapons to break through its hardened chalk armor layer. You must deal sufficient damage to force it out of its roaming state into its stationary, defensive "calcified shell" form.

Once encased in its shell, continue to shoot the Golem until it releases a massive dust cloud and exposes its core with an open-vent animation. Immediately sprint up to the exposed core and press the interaction key (E) to feed it Elemental Dust or Bio Toxin directly from your hotbar.

Stand back immediately after feeding, as the Golem will trigger a radial shockwave attack that stuns and deals heavy knockback. Do not confuse its normal arm-swing staggers with the core-venting phase, or you will take fatal melee damage.

Repeat the process of stripping its outer shell and feeding its core until the torpor meter fills completely and the Golem collapses unconscious. Open its inventory, insert Exceptional Kibble or high-tier meat, and protect it until the taming bar fills.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Fabricated Sniper Rifle or Longneck Rifle with plenty of ammunition; any accurate, high-damage ranged weapon works well for killing the attacking Vultures.; 1 Death Essence from a deceased, previously tamed adult creature capable of breeding. The creature stored in the Death Essence will be permanently consumed during the taming process.

inputs.label: None. The Oasisaur uses a defensive mini-game instead of conventional food taming

steps.text: Climb onto the wild Oasisaur's back and access the oasis inventory. Place a Death Essence inside to begin the tame; a baby clone of the deceased creature will appear in the oasis with health, wave, and taming-progress bars.

Immediately shoot down the Vultures that spawn and dive toward the baby. Clear each wave completely to advance the taming progress; the Vultures increase from roughly level 31 in the first wave to 61 in the second and 121 in the third.

Prioritize any Vulture that reaches the oasis—the baby is the actual failure condition, not the Oasisaur. If the baby takes too much damage and dies, the taming progress resets, forcing you to restart the process.

Kill every Vulture through the final wave until the orange taming-progress bar reaches 100%. The Oasisaur becomes instantly tamed with no knockout or feeding phase, while the creature represented by the Death Essence is permanently sacrificed.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Crossbow or Longneck Rifle with Tranq Darts (if needed for surrounding threats; not used on Cosmo directly).; Chitin (place in the last slot of your hotbar). Bug Repellant and Ghillie Armor are strongly recommended to avoid spooking it.

inputs.label: Chitin (Cosmo consumes Chitin directly from your hotbar to tame)

steps.text: Put on Ghillie Armor, apply Bug Repellant, and slowly crouch-walk toward the wild Cosmo from behind or the side to prevent drawing aggression or scaring it into fleeing.

Approach close enough for Cosmo to notice you without spooking. Watch for it to perform a distinct, friendly hovering or dancing animation with its web-shooters raised rather than a defensive retreat.
Approach Cosmo while it is performing its friendly animation and press the interaction key (E) to feed it Chitin directly from your last hotbar slot.
Back off slightly between feeds to avoid spooking it, then re-approach each time Cosmo resets its stance and signals for food. Continue hand-feeding Chitin until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None; Tidepup is a passive tame and should not be knocked unconscious.; A controllable tame or your own survivor to serve as the injured patient; use controlled damage, a Campfire, or Blood Extraction Syringes to drop health below 10%.

steps.text: Bring your chosen patient near the wild Tidepup and carefully reduce the survivor or tame to less than 10% of maximum health. Once the threshold is reached, the Tidepup's healing instinct will trigger.

Allow the Tidepup to approach and heal the critically injured target. After performing its healing animation, it becomes exhausted and enters a brief resting or "nap" state—this is your feeding window.

Approach the resting Tidepup and interact with it to feed Regular Kibble or your chosen meat. Do not attack or knock it out; if your patient dies before the healing cycle completes, you lose the setup and must trigger another healing opportunity.

Wait through the short cooldown, drop your survivor or tame below 10% health again, and let the Tidepup heal it. Feed the Tidepup each time it rests after healing and repeat until the taming meter reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None required; the Palaeoctopus uses a unique grab-and-feed knockout mechanic rather than conventional tranquilizer weapons.; **Bio Toxin or Narcotics** placed in the **last slot of your hotbar**. Bring Medical Brews to recover from the damage taken while being grabbed and bitten.

inputs.label: followed by Exceptional Kibble or other accepted carnivore foods

steps.text: Approach while the Palaeoctopus is resting and camouflaged rather than freely swimming. Move into range and intentionally allow its tentacles to seize you and pull you toward its beak.

Stay grabbed and watch closely for the heavy bite animation—the screen will shake as it prepares the real attack. Immediately press the interaction key to feed Bio Toxin or Narcotics from your last hotbar slot, raising the Palaeoctopus's torpor.

The Palaeoctopus performs several fake bite motions before the genuine feeding window. Do **not** spam the interaction key; feeding during a fake-out provides no torpor while you continue taking damage, so heal between grabs and wait specifically for the strong screen-shaking bite.

Repeat the grab-and-feed cycle until accumulated torpor finally knocks the Palaeoctopus unconscious. Immediately access its inventory and load it with Black Pearls or Exceptional Kibble, then maintain the knockout until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: High-damage weapons or a strong combat tame for killing Alpha Creatures during the trust phase.; Any Emote to attract the Parrot; optionally bring a Shovel for Treasure Cache objectives. No Narcotics or knockout supplies are required.

inputs.label: None. The Parrot uses a trust-based passive tame rather than Kibble or conventional feeding

steps.text: Approach a wild Parrot and perform any Emote, such as Wave. The Parrot will fly over and perch on your shoulder, immediately starting its roughly 1-hour taming timer.

While the Parrot rides your shoulder, raise its taming affinity by completing qualifying activities. Killing Alpha Creatures gives strong progress; digging up Treasure Caches and completing missions or collecting their reward crates also increase affinity.
Keep completing trust-building actions before the 1-hour window expires. Do not waste time attempting to feed or knock out the Parrot—neither method advances this tame.

Continue completing Alpha kills, Treasure Caches, or qualifying mission rewards until the Parrot's taming affinity reaches 100%. Once the bar fills, the Parrot becomes yours automatically with no final feeding or knockout step required.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Longneck Rifle with Tranquilizer Darts or Crossbow with Tranquilizer Arrows (none required if executing the fetch mechanic without knocking out).; Place your selected taming food in the far-right slot of your hotbar (Slot 0 / '0' key).

steps.text: Approach the wild Armadoggo without hostility. Look for it to curl into its armored ball stance or trigger a playful "fetch" animation where it drops an object near you.
Pick up the thrown or dropped object (such as a stick or ball item nearby) and throw it using your primary action button to initiate the passive taming minigame.

Wait for the Armadoggo to retrieve the item and return it to you in a docile, happy state. Immediately approach it and press the interaction key (E) to feed it the food item placed in your far-right hotbar slot.

Repeat the fetch-and-feed process each time the creature brings the item back. Keep wild predators away from the area so the Armadoggo is not startled into a combat state, which resets taming progress, until the taming meter reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Crossbow or Longneck Rifle loaded with Tranquilizer Darts/Arrows (or a low-damage Club for lower levels).; Narcotic or Narcoberries (though rarely needed due to high base torpor drain resistance once unconscious).

inputs.label: Sweet Vegetable Cake (the only food item an Achatina will accept for taming and eating)

steps.text: Locate a wild Achatina in swampy or redwood biomes and clear out surrounding predators like Kaprosuchus and Titanoboa to ensure a safe environment.

Shoot the soft, exposed flesh of the head or body with tranquilizer ammo. Avoid hitting its shell, as the shell grants massive damage resistance and causes the Achatina to retreat inside, drastically reducing torpor gain per shot.

Maintain a steady firing pace to knock it out without accidentally killing it, as its low health pool makes high-tier weapons risky. If it retracts completely into its shell, pause your attacks briefy until it pokes its body back out to avoid wasting ammo or dealing lethal shell-impact damage.

Once the Achatina falls unconscious, open its inventory and insert your Sweet Vegetable Cakes. It will passively consume the cakes until tamed; ensure you keep extra cakes in its inventory after taming so it does not starve.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Crossbow or Longneck Rifle loaded with Tranquilizer Arrows or Tranquilizer Darts.; Narcotics, Narcoberries, or Bio Toxin (Allosaurus torpor drains at a moderate rate).

steps.text: Locate the Allosaurus pack and identify the high-level target. Eliminate the lower-level pack mates first to strip the dominant pack leader of its red glowing alpha buff, extra damage, and slow-inflicting bleed attacks.

Position yourself on a high cliff, rock ledge, or high-tier mount where the remaining Allosaurus cannot reach you. Its high movement speed makes ground-based kite-taming dangerous without a speed investment.
Fire tranquilizer projectiles directly at the target's head to maximize torpor gain. Keep a steady firing rhythm to account for its rapid torpor depletion and prevent torpor decay between shots.

Continue shooting until the Allosaurus turns to flee, then land the final tranquilizer shots to render it unconscious. Access its inventory, insert Superior Kibble or Raw Mutton, and manage its torpor levels using Narcotics until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Crossbow or Harpoon Gun (bows do not work underwater).; Tranquilizer Arrows or Spear Bolts for knockout; Scuba Gear or Lazarus Chowder for oxygen management.

steps.text: Locate an Anglerfish in the deep ocean and attack it to draw aggression. Swim backward toward underwater caves or shallower reefs where dangerous deep-sea predators like Tusoteuthis and Mosasaurs cannot follow.

Fire Tranquilizer Arrows or Spear Bolts continuously while swimming backward. The Anglerfish moves quickly and has a small hit box, so use Scuba Flippers to stay ahead of its melee range and avoid taking heavy damage.
Watch for the Anglerfish to turn around and flee at high torpor. Immediately give chase while continuing to land shots,

Continue firing until the creature floats motionless underwater. Open its inventory immediately, insert Exceptional Kibble or Raw Mutton, and protect it from surrounding Megalodons or Cnidaria while it eats

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Longneck Rifle with Tranquilizer Darts (or Shocking Tranq Darts) / Crossbow with Tranquilizer Arrows.; Narcotics or Narcoberries (for torpor maintenance), Parachute or Grappling Hook (for aerial or cliffside shooting).

steps.text: Position yourself on a nearby cliff, rock formation, or tamed flyer where the slow-moving Ankylosaurus cannot reach you.
Aim directly for the Ankylo's head using your tranquilizer darts or arrows to maximize torpor damage, taking advantage of its extremely slow base movement speed.
Maintain safe spacing if taming on foot; if the Ankylo closes the distance, backpedal continuously to avoid its heavy tail-club knockback and melee damage.

Continue shooting until the creature turns to flee and collapses unconscious. Once downed, immediately open its inventory, insert your preferred taming food along with Narcotics to keep its torpor high, and protect it until taming completes.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Crossbow or Longneck Rifle paired with Tranq Darts, or a simple Chitin/Gillie-equipped player with a Wooden Club (if low level).; Bola (essential for keeping it grounded), Rare Flower (optional, to force aggression if it flees).

steps.text: Locate the Archaeopteryx climbing up tree trunks or gliding short distances, and immediately throw a Bola to pin it down before it can escape into the canopy.
Fire Tranq Darts or Tranq Arrows directly at its body while it is bound; its extremely low health pool makes headshots or high-grade weapons risky as you can easily kill it.
Once knocked unconscious, closely monitor its torpor bar as it drains at a steady rate relative to its low maximum torpor capacity.
Open the unconscious creature's inventory and place Simple Kibble or Chitin inside, staying nearby to guard it from forest predators until the taming meter reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Crossbow or Longneck Rifle loaded with Tranquilizer Arrows or Tranquilizer Darts.; Narcotics or Bio Toxin for torpor management, and a Flying Mount or Bolas/Bear Trap (optional) to disable or safely position yourself.

steps.text: Locate an Argentavis away from dangerous predators like Alpha raptors or Sabertooths. Draw its attention with a ranged shot, as its slow flight speed makes it easy to kite while walking or riding a mount backward.

Fire tranquilizer projectiles into its head for maximum torpor damage, pacing your shots every 5 seconds to let the torpor build up efficiently. Keep moving backward to avoid its melee attacks and prevent it from pinning you.

Watch for the Argentavis to turn around and attempt to fly away when its torpor nears maximum. Immediately sprint after it or use a fast flying mount to stay within range and land the final tranquilizer shots before it escapes into hazardous terrain.

Once knocked out, clear the surrounding area of carnivores to protect its low health pool. Open its inventory, insert Superior Kibble or Raw Mutton, and monitor its torpor level with Narcotics until the taming bar fills.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Crossbow or Longneck Rifle loaded with Tranquilizer Darts/Arrows.; Bug Repellant (essential) and Ghillie Armor to minimize detection.

inputs.label: Raw Mutton/Raw Meat placed in the far-right slot of your hotbar

steps.text: Equip full Ghillie Armor and apply Bug Repellant before entering the creature's sightline. Place your preferred taming food into the last slot of your hotbar.
Crouch or crawl directly behind the Aberrant Arthropleura. Approach strictly from its rear to avoid triggering its aggressive aggro radius or wide-range acid spit attack.
Carefully move close enough to prompt the "Feed [Item]" interaction text on its tail segment. Press the interaction key to hand-feed the creature without hitting or bumping into its hitboxes.

Immediately retreat straight backward after feeding to break line of sight before its passive timer resets. Wait for its hunger to drop again, maintain your stealth buffs, and repeat the passive feeding process until tamed.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Crossbow or Longneck Rifle loaded with Tranquilizer Darts/Arrows. Harpoon Gun with Net Projectile (strongly recommended for easy immobilization).; Narcotics or Bio Toxin for torpor maintenance (Baryonyx has a moderate torpor drain rate).

inputs.label: Raw Prime Fish Meat. (Note: Baryonyx only eats fish meat)

steps.text: Lure the Baryonyx onto dry land using a ranged weapon or crossbow. Immediately fire a Net Projectile to trap it for 60 seconds, or use standard kiting tactics to keep distance.
Never fight or attempt to tame a Baryonyx while swimming in water. In water, it executes a devastating 360-degree tail-spin attack that permanently stuns and dismounts you until you drown.
While it is netted or trapped on land, fire Tranquilizer Darts or Arrows into its head to maximize torpor damage. Keep firing steadily until the Baryonyx turns to flee or falls unconscious.

Once knocked out, open its inventory and place Regular Kibble or Raw Prime Fish Meat inside. Monitor its torpor levels using Narcotics/Bio Toxin and clear surrounding aggressive predators while it completes the taming process.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Crossbow or Harpoon Gun with Tranquilizer Darts/Spear Bolts (optional, only needed for clearing surrounding mantas).; Scuba Gear or Lazarus Chowder for oxygen management; Water Mount (like a Megalodon or Basilosaurus) or Aquatic Crossbow to clear aggressive ocean fauna.

inputs.label: Raw Prime Meat. Place the chosen food in the last slot of your hotbar

steps.text: Locate a wild Basilosaurus near the surface and eliminate its aggressive escort of Mantas and Megalodons using a water mount or ranged weapons. Ensure all hostiles are dead so they do not interrupt the passive taming process or damage you.

Swim up to the Basilosaurus safely—it is naturally non-hostile to players. Target its head or mouth area, make sure your taming food is in your far-right hotbar slot, and press the interaction key (E) to feed it.
Track the creature's hunger meter and wait out the cooldown between feedings. Stay close to the surface, as Basilosaurus passively takes constant damage if it dives into deep water.

Never accidentally hit the Basilosaurus during or after clearing the mantas, as taking damage will reset its taming effectiveness and cause nearby ocean predators to re-aggro. Repeat the passive feeding prompt until the taming meter reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None; the Onyc is a passive tame and is torpor-immune, so Tranq Arrows and Tranq Darts will not work.; Bug Repellant (strongly recommended) and Ghillie Armor as extra protection. Place the taming food in the very last slot of your hotbar; you must be at least level 65 to feed it.

steps.text: Use Bug Repellant before approaching the Onyc to prevent it from immediately aggroing onto you. Move toward it carefully with your preferred meat in the last hotbar slot; do not attack it or attempt to knock it unconscious.
Approach until the passive-feed prompt appears, then press the interaction key (E) to give it the food. Back away afterward and wait until it becomes hungry enough for the next feeding.

phases.name: Do Not Touch or Aggro It

steps.text: Bug Repellant does not protect you if you physically bump into the Onyc, and it cannot be fed while attacking another creature or feeding on a corpse. If it becomes aggressive, retreat until it completely loses aggro before approaching again; its attacks can also inflict Mega Rabies.
Reapply Bug Repellant as needed and approach each time the feeding prompt returns. Keep feeding Raw Mutton or your chosen alternative until the taming meter reaches 100% and the Onyc becomes yours.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Crossbow or Longneck Rifle (loaded with Tranquilizer Darts or Shocking Tranquilizer Darts).; Narcotics, Bio Toxin, or Narcoberries (Castoroides drain torpor rapidly), Bola, and a Flying Mount (optional, for safe high-ground tranquilizing).

steps.text: Target a lone Castoroides away from its pack and throw a Bola at its feet to trap it for 30 seconds. Alternatively, grab it with an Argentavis and drop it into a safe, isolated area on land.

Immediately unload Tranq Darts or Tranq Arrows into its head to build up torpor before the Bola wears off. Aim strictly for headshots to maximize torpor gain and minimize health damage to the creature.

Monitor its torpor closely, as the Castoroides has an extremely fast torpor depletion rate compared to its health pool. Continuously pump Narcotics or Bio Toxin into its inventory to keep it knocked out cold, as it will wake up quickly if neglected.
Access its inventory while unconscious and deposit Superior Kibble or Crops. Keep the Castoroides defended from nearby predators until the taming bar fills completely.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None. Do not use tranquilizers or damage the Gigantopithecus; it is a passive tame.; Place the taming food in the very last slot of your hotbar. No Narcotics or torpor-maintenance items are required.

steps.text: Put your food in the last hotbar slot and carefully move behind the Gigantopithecus until the feeding prompt appears. Press the interaction key (E) to give it its first piece of food.
Stay behind it as it wanders and wait for its hunger to drop enough for another feeding. Move back into feeding range whenever the prompt returns and immediately give it another piece.

Do not bump into, stand directly in front of, or attack the Gigantopithecus—it will become aggressive if you invade its personal space. If it aggroes, run away and break line of sight until it calms down; your taming progress remains, but fighting back can reduce taming effectiveness.

Continue following from behind and feeding whenever prompted until the taming bar reaches 100%. The Gigantopithecus will automatically become yours with no knockout or inventory-feeding phase required.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None. Titanoboa is a passive tame and must not be attacked or aggroed during the feeding process.; Multiple Fertilized Eggs carried in your **player inventory**. Drop them yourself near the Titanoboa; eggs dropped from a mount's inventory will be ignored.

inputs.label: Fertilized Giganotosaurus Eggs (preferred) > Fertilized Bronto/Diplodocus Eggs > Fertilized Rex/Quetzal/Dimetrodon Eggs > other Fertilized Eggs. Unfertilized eggs do not work

steps.text: Get close enough to place an egg near the Titanoboa without causing it to attack you or another creature. It will only accept eggs while calm and not distracted by combat.
Drop a Fertilized Egg directly from your own inventory near the Titanoboa. When ready, it will move to the egg, perform an attack-like animation, consume it, and gain taming progress.

Back away after each egg and wait for the next feeding interval. Do not attack it, let it aggro onto you, or distract it with another target; also never substitute unfertilized eggs or drop the eggs from a mount's inventory.

Continue dropping Fertilized Eggs whenever the Titanoboa is ready to eat again until the taming bar reaches 100%. The Titanoboa will automatically become yours after the final egg—no knockout, Narcotics, or inventory feeding is required.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Crossbow, Longneck Rifle, or Tek Rifle (strictly to kill wild dinos for corpses).; Large creature corpses (Yutyrannus, Rex, Bronto, or Diplodocus provide the fastest progress). Heavy Drag-capable mount or high-movement-speed gear recommended.

steps.text: Kill a high-drag-weight creature near the Carcharodontosaurus and drag its corpse toward the Carchar while holding down the interaction key. Avoid getting too close to the Carchar while holding the body, as it will attack if you bump into it.

Sniff out the Carchar's neutral state; drop or present the body near its head. When the Carchar notices the offering, it will perform a sniffing animation and eat the corpse, filling its trust meter with a green indicator.

Repeat the corpse-feeding process until the trust meter fills completely and the Carchar becomes temporarily rideable. Immediately press the interaction key to jump onto its back before the timer expires.

Once mounted, sprint around and slaughter as many wild creatures as possible to fill its frenzy meter to 100% before the time limit runs out. Reaching full frenzy finalizes the trust bond, permanently taming the Carcharodontosaurus and booting you off with your new tame.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Crossbow or Longneck Rifle (loaded with Tranq Arrows or Tranquilizer Darts).; Narcotics, Bio Toxin, or Narcoberries to maintain torpor levels while unconscious.

steps.text: High-ground is key—sprint to a rock or cliff node out of reach, or trap the Carnotaurus in a 2x2 stone doorway trap. Because of its fast movement speed and high knockback, do not attempt to kite it on flat foot.

Fire your tranquillizer projectiles steady and clean, waiting roughly 5 seconds between shots to let the torpor-over-time fully build up. Aim for the head to inflict maximum torpor per hit and conserve ammunition.

Keep a close eye on the Carnotaurus's health, especially if using a Crossbow, as its lower total health pool makes it vulnerable to accidental death. Once its torpor nears maximum, it will turn and flee wildly—chase it down quickly to land the final knock-out shot before it aggros onto nearby predators.

Once the Carno falls unconscious, open its inventory immediately and place Regular Kibble or Raw Mutton inside. Monitor its torpor bar closely and force-feed Narcotics as needed to keep it asleep until the taming bar hits 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None (Knockout/Torpor weapons will damage or kill it).; Ghillie Suit (essential for stealth) and Beer Jar. Place the Beer Jar in the last slot of your hotbar.

inputs.label: followed by Stimberry or Majorberry (significantly slower)

steps.text: Put on a full set of Ghillie Suit armor and approach the wild Chalicotherium slowly from behind. Crouch or prone to avoid drawing its visual aggression.
Move within interaction range of its hindquarters while it is calm or idle. Press the interaction key (E) to feed it a Beer Jar directly from your last hotbar slot.

Immediately back away after feeding, as the Chalicotherium will turn aggressive if you linger in its line of sight. Wait out the feeding cooldown from a safe distance until it returns to a calm wandering state.

Re-approach from behind and repeat the passive feeding cycle each time it becomes hungry. Maintain stealth to avoid triggering its mud-flinging rock attack, which will reset your taming progress, until the tame hits 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None required.; Fish Basket (must be crafted and placed on your hotbar).

inputs.label: None (The Coelacanth is captured instantly at 100% taming progress)

steps.text: Scout bodies of water for a Coelacanth, keeping an eye out for larger size multipliers (e.g., 1.5x to 2.
Submerge yourself in the water, equip the Fish Basket from your hotbar, and place it on the river or ocean floor directly next to the Coelacanth.
Wait for the Coelacanth to swim close enough to the basket, then target the Fish Basket and press the interaction key (E) to trap it inside.
Open your inventory to pick up the filled Fish Basket before its quick expiration timer runs out. Place the filled basket on your hotbar and activate it anywhere in the water to release your

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Wooden Club, Crossbow/Bow with Tranquilizer Arrows, or Equus.; Extra Prime Meat (drops spoil quickly; bring a Preserving Bin or Hyena/Oviraptor storage if taming on-site). No torpor maintenance needed once down due to small torpor pool and fast tame rate.

inputs.label: Raw Prime Meat (heavily preferred) or Raw Prime Fish Meat. Note: Compies refuse regular Raw Meat

steps.text: Locate the Compy and count its companions. Compies gain a "Pack Leader" damage and aggression buff when two or more are together; isolate a single Compy or eliminate the rest of the pack with melee weapons before attempting the knock out.

Allow the single Compy to run toward you and strike it with a Wooden Club or fire a single Tranquilizer Arrow to its body. Because of its tiny health and torpor pool, higher-tier weapons like Longneck Rifles will easily kill it,

Stand over the unconscious Compy immediately upon it hitting the ground. Its torpor drops extremely fast, but its food bar drains rapidly enough that it will begin eating almost instantly if top-tier food is present.

Open the Compy's inventory and place Raw Prime Meat inside. Do not use standard Raw Meat, as it will ignore it completely; it will consume the Prime Meat quickly, finishing the tame in a matter of seconds.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Crossbow or Compound Bow (to clear surrounding hostile creatures).; Parachute or Grappling Hooks, Water Jar/Canteen (for hydration), and Chitin/Flint if you need on-the-fly armor repairs.

inputs.label: Primal Crystal (preferred, mined from adult Crystal Wyverns) or standard Crystal. Place this item in the far-right slot of your hotbar

steps.text: Locate a passive Blood Crystal Wyvern flying low or resting on the ground. Crouch to lower your visibility profile and approach its legs or hindquarters from behind to avoid startling it into flight.

Walk up to its feet and press the interaction key (E) to feed a Primal Crystal or Crystal from your last hotbar slot. Alternatively, jump onto its back/wings while it is grounded so you remain on top of it when it takes off.

If the Wyvern takes flight while you are riding its back, stay crouched or prone in the dip between its shoulders and wings to prevent slipping off. Keep your crosshairs on its body and continue pressing the interaction key every time it becomes hungry.

Repeat the feeding process each time the on-screen prompt appears until the taming bar hits 100%. Use a parachute or grappling hook if you are thrown off mid-air, otherwise ride it safely to the ground once tamed.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None required for the tame itself; Ember Crystal Wyverns are passive-tamed. Bring armor or a weapon only as protection if one becomes aggressive.; Reach at least **Survivor Level 65** and place your taming food in the **last slot of your hotbar**. Make sure you are targeting a normal Ember Crystal Wyvern, not an aggressive **Crystal Wyvern Heir**, which cannot be tamed.

inputs.label: **Primal Crystal** (strongly preferred) or regular Crystal. Primal Crystal provides substantially faster taming and higher effectiveness

steps.text: Move up to a normal wild Ember Crystal Wyvern without attacking it. These Wyverns are normally passive unless provoked, allowing you to get close enough to begin feeding.

phases.name: Feed From the Last Hotbar Slot

steps.text: With Primal Crystal equipped in your final hotbar slot, get close to the Wyvern and press the interaction key (E) when the feeding prompt appears. After each feed, stay near it and wait for the next feeding interval.

Do not strike the Wyvern or otherwise provoke it; an angry Ember Crystal Wyvern will retaliate with its damaging fire breath and interrupt your clean passive-tame cycle. Also verify that it is not a Crystal Wyvern Heir, as Heirs are permanently aggressive and untameable.

Follow the Wyvern and feed another Primal Crystal every time the prompt becomes available. Continue the passive-feed cycle until the taming bar reaches 100%, at which point the Ember Crystal Wyvern is immediately yours and requires no saddle to ride.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None required; the Tropical Crystal Wyvern is a passive tame and should not be attacked.; Reach at least **Survivor Level 65** and place your taming food in the **last slot of your hotbar**. A Parachute or Grappling Hook can help if you ride or grapple onto the Wyvern while following it.

inputs.label: **Primal Crystal** (preferred) or regular Crystal. Primal Crystal tames significantly faster and with better effectiveness

steps.text: Walk up to a normal wild Tropical Crystal Wyvern without attacking it. These Wyverns are passive unless provoked, allowing you to move close enough for the feeding prompt.
With Primal Crystal in your final hotbar slot, press the interaction key (E) when the feeding prompt appears. After the feed, stay with the Wyvern and wait for it to become hungry again.

phases.name: Do Not Confuse It With an Heir

steps.text: Avoid **Tropical Crystal Wyvern Heirs**; they are aggressive and cannot be tamed. Do not attack your normal target either, as provoking it can turn an easy passive tame into a dangerous chase.

Follow the Tropical Crystal Wyvern and feed another Primal Crystal every time the prompt returns. Continue the passive-feed cycle until the taming bar reaches 100%, at which point it immediately becomes yours and can be ridden without a saddle.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Crossbow or Longneck Rifle loaded with Tranquilizer Arrows or Tranquilizer Darts.; Large quantities of Narcotics or Bio Toxin to sustain torpor, and a high-tier Carnivore mount to rapidly collect fresh meat during the feeding phase.

steps.text: Locate the Daeodon and kill off its surrounding pack mates or nearby predators to prevent interference during the knockout. Ensure you keep your distance, as its passive healing ring will rapidly heal nearby aggressive wild dinos.
Fire tranq darts or arrows consistently into the Daeodon's head to rapidly scale its torpor. Maintain a steady cadence, as its torpor drain rate is moderately fast.

Once unconscious, monitor its food meter closely; the Daeodon consumes food at an extremely rapid pace once tamed or sleeping due to its massive natural hunger stat. Do not let its inventory run out of food, or its taming effectiveness will drop dramatically.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Wooden Club, Slingshot (with Stone ammo), or Bow (with Tranq Arrows).; None required for passive hotbar interaction.

steps.text: Approach the Dilophosaur from a safe distance and dodge its slow, telegraphed spit attack, which will temporarily blind and slow you if hit.

Fire Tranq Arrows or Slingshot stones into its head, or close the distance and strike it repeatedly with a Wooden Club. Due to its very low base health and torpor pool, be careful not to accidentally kill it with over-damaging weapons like Crossbows.
Monitor the unconscious Dilo closely. Because its torpor drains quickly relative to its total pool, force-feed it Narcoberries or Narcotics if the taming progress takes longer than expected.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Crossbow, Longneck Rifle, or Electric Prod (for instant high torpor).; Bio Toxin, Narcotics, or Narcoberries (massive quantities required due to ultra-fast torpor drop).

steps.text: Locate the Dimetrodon, clear surrounding swamp predators, and immobilize it using a Bolas or net projectile. Since they have low health pools, use a high-quality Crossbow with Tranquilizer Darts or a Longneck Rifle with Shocking Tranq Darts to avoid accidentally killing it.
Rapidly fire tranquilizers into the target until it drops unconscious. Be prepared for its torpor bar to drain at an exceptionally rapid rate the second it hits the ground.

Immediately open its inventory upon knockout and spam Narcotics or Bio Toxin to keep its torpor topped off. Never leave its side during the process, as missing even a short window of torpor maintenance will result in it waking up and resetting progress.
Place Exceptional Kibble or Raw Mutton into its inventory alongside the torpor supplies.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Crossbow or Longneck Rifle loaded with Tranquilizer Darts/Arrows (Bola recommended for immobilizing).; Bola (essential for keeping it grounded), Narcotics or Bio Toxin for torpor maintenance.

steps.text: Locate a landed or low-flying Dimorphodon and throw a Bola directly at it to trap it in place for 30 seconds.

Aim carefully at its body or head with your Crossbow or Longneck Rifle, firing tranquilizers steadily. Due to its extremely low base health, pause briefly between shots to avoid accidentally killing it before it drops.

Be aware that attacking one Dimorphodon will instantly draw aggression from any nearby pack members, which will swarm and attack you directly rather than your mount. Clear out any surrounding flock first or be ready to dodge their rapid head-strikes while keeping your target Bola'd.

Once its torpor maxes out, the Dimorphodon will fall unconscious. Open its inventory, insert Regular Kibble or Raw Prime Meat, and monitor its quickly depleting torpor with Narcotics until the tame completes.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Longneck Rifle with Tranq Darts (preferred); Crossbow with Tranq Arrows as a riskier alternative due to the Diplocaulus’s low health.; Bola to immobilize it; Narcotics or Narcoberries if torpor maintenance is needed.

inputs.label: Simple Kibble (preferred) or Raw Fish Meat / Raw Meat

steps.text: Approach and immediately throw a Bola to stop it from fleeing. Diplocaulus are skittish and will attempt to escape rather than fight, making immobilization the easiest way to line up clean shots.
Shoot it with Tranq Darts, spacing your shots to let the torpor build. Its health is relatively low compared with its torpor, so a Longneck Rifle is safer than repeatedly hitting it with a Crossbow.

Do not spam Tranq Arrows or continue firing once it begins collapsing. High-damage Crossbows can kill higher-level Diplocaulus before enough torpor is applied, especially if it has already taken damage.
Once unconscious, access its inventory and load it with Simple Kibble or Raw Fish Meat. Monitor its torpor and force-feed Narcotics or Narcoberries if necessary until the taming bar completes.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None required. Avoid damaging the Diplodocus if using the preferred passive-taming method.; Place your taming food in the very last slot of your hotbar so it can be fed with the interaction key.

inputs.label: other Berries. Vegetables cannot be used for the passive tame

steps.text: Walk directly up to the conscious Diplodocus with Regular Kibble or berries in your last hotbar slot. When the feeding prompt appears, press the interaction key (E) to give it its first piece of food.

After noticing you, the Diplodocus will repeatedly swing its body and shove you away. These attacks deal no direct damage, so stay close—standing underneath or between its front legs can make it much easier to remain within feeding range.

Do not mistake its pushing behavior for damaging aggression; the real danger is being knocked off a cliff, into hostile creatures, or far enough away to interrupt your tame. After the first feeding, expect a longer initial wait before it becomes hungry enough to accept another piece.

Remain near the Diplodocus and watch for the feeding prompt to reappear. Feed it again every time it becomes hungry, repeating the process until the taming bar reaches 100% and the Diplodocus becomes yours.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Longneck Rifle with Tranquilizer Darts or Shocking Tranquilizer Darts preferred; Crossbow with Tranq Arrows only if necessary.; Narcotics or Bio Toxin for torpor maintenance. Dire Bears have unusually high torpor compared to their health, so higher-quality darts are strongly recommended to reduce the chance of killing them during knockout.

steps.text: Engage the Dire Bear from a position where it cannot easily reach you and begin landing Tranquilizer Darts. Keep your shots controlled rather than firing as quickly as possible.

Space your shots slightly to allow the delayed torpor from each dart to apply before firing again. Dire Bears have relatively low health for the amount of torpor required to knock them out, so unnecessary extra hits can kill the bear before it drops.

Watch carefully as the Dire Bear begins fleeing from high torpor. Do not switch to damaging weapons or recklessly spam Tranq Arrows during the final stretch; continue using high torpor-to-damage ammunition until it collapses.

Once the Dire Bear falls unconscious, immediately stop firing and access its inventory. Load it with Superior Kibble, Giant Bee Honey, or your best available meat, then use Narcotics or Bio Toxin as needed to keep its torpor above zero until the tame completes.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Longneck Rifle with Tranq Darts (preferred) or Crossbow with Tranq Arrows.; Narcotics, Narcoberries, or Bio Toxin for maintaining torpor after knockout.

inputs.label: Superior Kibble (preferred) or Raw Mutton / Raw Prime Meat / Raw Meat

steps.text: Separate the Direwolf you want from any surrounding pack members, then aggro it and begin firing Tranq Darts or Tranq Arrows. Keep enough distance to avoid its fast melee attacks while maintaining clear shots.

Continue landing tranquilizer shots, allowing a few seconds between hits for torpor to rise. Direwolves have relatively low health compared with their torpor requirement, so avoid unnecessary damaging shots or rapid-fire arrows that could kill the target.

As its torpor approaches the knockout threshold, the Direwolf will attempt to flee. Keep pressure on it and land your remaining tranq shots without switching to damaging weapons or letting it escape into additional threats.

Once the Direwolf falls unconscious, access its inventory and load it with Superior Kibble or meat. Monitor its torpor and force-feed Narcotics, Narcoberries, or Bio Toxin as needed until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Fists, Wooden Club, or Slingshot. Avoid stronger weapons or excessive Tranq Arrow shots—the Dodo has very low health and is easy to kill accidentally.; Narcotics or Narcoberries are optional for higher-level Dodos when using slower foods; usually unnecessary when using Basic Kibble.

steps.text: Approach the Dodo and repeatedly punch it, strike it with a Wooden Club, or hit it with Slingshot stones. Aim for the head when using a Slingshot to build torpor quickly.
The Dodo may attempt to run as its torpor rises. Stay close and continue landing controlled hits until it collapses unconscious.
Stop attacking immediately once the Dodo drops. Its tiny health pool makes stronger weapons and unnecessary extra hits extremely likely to kill it instead of completing the knockout.

Access the unconscious Dodo's inventory and place Basic Kibble, Crops, Mejoberries, or other Berries inside. Let it eat automatically, using Narcotics or Narcoberries only if its torpor gets dangerously low before the taming bar finishes.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: High-damage weapons or powerful combat tames capable of killing the DodoRex. Zomdodos themselves do not require tranquilizers or damage to tame.; None. No Narcotics, Bolas, traps, or passive-feeding items are required; the tame is completed with the interaction key after the DodoRex dies.

steps.text: While the DodoRex is active, nearby Zomdodos are hostile and cannot be claimed. Avoid killing the specific Zomdodos you want while dealing with the encounter.
Defeat the DodoRex completely. Once it dies, any surviving Zomdodos associated with it lose their hostility and become passive.
Ignore normal Dodo taming methods—Tranq Arrows, clubs, berries, and Kibble are unnecessary. The claim window only exists after the DodoRex has been killed.
Approach a surviving passive Zomdodo and press the interaction key (E) to instantly claim it. No feeding, knockout, taming bar, or additional waiting is required.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None. The DodoRex is **torpor immune** and cannot be knocked out or conventionally tamed.; Event-specific summoning currency and a Cooking Pot. During applicable events, the required resource has historically included **Wishbones, Coal, Bunny Eggs, or Birthday Cake**, depending on the event/version.

inputs.label: None. The DodoRex does not use kibble

steps.text: Do not attempt to tranquilize or passive-feed a naturally spawned DodoRex. Wild event DodoRexes are boss creatures and cannot be converted through normal taming mechanics.

During an event that allows acquisition, gather the required event resource and place it into a Cooking Pot. The exact currency and quantity depend on the active event; Turkey Trial versions, for example, have used Wishbones.
Craft the DodoRex summon from the Cooking Pot. Do not waste Tranq Darts, Narcotics, or food attempting to tame the hostile version—the creature is torpor immune.

The event-summoned DodoRex appears already tamed/claimable and can be ridden without a saddle. Treat it as a **temporary event tame**; summoned versions historically disappear after their event-specific timer expires rather than becoming a permanent conventional tame.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Longneck Rifle with Tranquilizer Darts (preferred) or Crossbow with Tranquilizer Arrows.; Narcotics, Bio Toxin, or Narcoberries for maintaining torpor after knockout.

steps.text: Fire Tranquilizer Darts or Arrows into the Doedicurus's head for maximum torpor efficiency. Keep landing controlled shots while it remains mobile and exposed.

phases.name: Keep It Out of Its Shell

steps.text: As its health drops, the Doedicurus can curl into a defensive ball, massively reducing incoming damage and torpor gain. Space your tranquilizer shots to let torpor build without unnecessarily shredding its health.

Do not waste ammunition firing into a fully curled Doedicurus; the heavy damage reduction makes further torpor application extremely inefficient. Back off and wait for it to uncurl before continuing your knockout shots.

Continue firing tranquilizers whenever it is exposed until it falls unconscious. Access its inventory, load it with Regular Kibble or your best available vegetables/berries, and use Narcotics or Bio Toxin as needed to keep its torpor above zero until the tame completes.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None; the Ichthyosaurus is a non-violent passive tame and should not be attacked.; No narcotics or torpor items are required. Place your chosen taming food in the very last slot of your hotbar.

steps.text: Swim toward the wild Ichthyosaurus with your taming food ready. Ichthyosaurs are naturally curious and will often swim directly toward you, making the first feed easy to land.

When the interaction prompt appears, press the interaction key (E) to feed it from the last slot of your hotbar. The first feed starts the taming process; wait until it becomes hungry again before attempting another feed.

Follow the Ichthyosaurus as it swims around, because it may suddenly wander away between feeding intervals. Do not attack or tranquilize it, and watch for hostile aquatic creatures such as Megalodons or Mantas that can interrupt the tame.

Each time the feeding prompt returns, swim alongside the Ichthyosaurus and feed it again. Continue feeding Simple Kibble or your chosen meat until the taming bar reaches 100% and the Ichthyosaurus becomes yours.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None required; the Dung Beetle is a passive tame.; Place the chosen feces in the **last slot of your hotbar**. Bring extra pieces because multiple passive feeds are required.

inputs.label: Spoiled Meat. **Massive Animal Feces cannot be used.**

steps.text: Walk up to the wild Dung Beetle without damaging it. It is a passive tame, so knocking it unconscious is unnecessary and attacking it will interrupt the process.
Put Large Animal Feces in your final hotbar slot, move close enough for the interaction prompt, and press the interaction key (E) to feed it. Large Animal Feces provides the preferred taming food.
Back away after feeding and wait for the next feeding prompt. Do not hit or otherwise aggravate the beetle; aggression can delay the next available feed by several minutes.
Return each time the feeding prompt becomes available and feed another piece of feces. Continue the passive-feed cycle until the taming bar reaches 100% and the Dung Beetle becomes yours.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Crossbow with Tranq Arrows, or Harpoon Launcher with Tranq Spear Bolts.; SCUBA Gear for sustained underwater pursuit; Narcotics or Bio Toxin to maintain torpor after knockout.

steps.text: Equip your Crossbow or Harpoon Launcher and repeatedly hit the Dunkleosteus with tranquilizing ammunition. Keep enough distance to avoid its powerful bite while maintaining clear shots.

Continue firing as it swims after you, allowing a few seconds between hits for torpor to build. Its armored body heavily reduces incoming damage, so expect the knockout to require considerably more ammunition than similarly sized aquatic creatures.

Once its torpor gets high, the Dunkleosteus will attempt to flee instead of fighting. Chase it and keep landing tranquilizer hits, but avoid switching to damaging weapons or recklessly spamming shots after it is close to dropping.

Once the Dunkleosteus falls unconscious, access its inventory and load it with Superior Kibble, Raw Mutton, or Raw Prime Meat. Monitor its torpor and force-feed Narcotics or Bio Toxin if necessary until the tame completes.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: No weapons required; use a Basilosaurus as your safest taming mount because it can absorb the Electrophorus’ electrical attacks without being stunned or slowed.; SCUBA Gear for underwater breathing and Bio Toxin placed in the very last slot of your hotbar. Stimulants can help counter torpor if you are shocked while dismounted.

steps.text: Approach the Electrophorus while mounted on a Basilosaurus and allow it to aggro onto you. Let it discharge its electrical shock against the Basilo instead of exposing your survivor directly.

Immediately after the Electrophorus releases its shock, dismount while its electrical attack is recharging. Swim close, press the interaction key (E) to feed it Bio Toxin from your last hotbar slot, then remount your Basilosaurus.

Do not remain beside the Electrophorus after feeding. Its attacks inflict torpor and its electrical shock can heavily slow you, making repeated hits increasingly dangerous; remount before the next discharge and repeat the shock-feed cycle.

Continue letting the Electrophorus discharge into your Basilosaurus, dismounting during each recharge window, and feeding Bio Toxin whenever the passive-tame prompt becomes available. Repeat until the final feed completes the tame—do not knock it unconscious.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None. The Unicorn is a non-violent passive tame; attacking or knocking it unconscious will not tame it.; Ghillie Armor to approach without spooking it. Place the taming food in the very last slot of your hotbar before approaching.

inputs.label: Simple Kibble (preferred) or Rockarrot / Crops / Mejoberries

steps.text: Crouch toward the Unicorn while wearing Ghillie Armor and avoid startling it. Once the feeding prompt appears, press the interaction key (E) to give it food from your last hotbar slot, then immediately press E again to mount it.

Stay mounted as the wild Unicorn runs uncontrollably. When it begins bucking and the on-screen feeding prompt appears, press E **once** to feed it and remain mounted; each successful feeding increases taming progress.

Never spam E or press it before the Unicorn bucks, as an extra interaction can dismount you. Missing the feeding window also throws you off, causes the Unicorn to kick you for torpor, and reduces taming effectiveness.

Continue riding and feeding the Unicorn every time it bucks until the taming bar reaches 100%. Once the final feeding completes, the Unicorn automatically becomes yours—no knockout, Narcotics, or additional claiming step is required.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Bola, Crossbow with Tranq Arrows, or preferably a Longneck Rifle with Tranquilizer Darts to reduce the risk of killing it.; Narcotics, Bio Toxin, or Narcoberries; Gallimimus loses torpor very quickly, so bring plenty and be ready to force-feed them immediately after knockout.

steps.text: Get close enough to land a Bola and stop it from sprinting away. Once restrained, immediately begin applying torpor before the Bola wears off.

Use Tranq Darts or spaced Tranq Arrow shots to raise torpor while minimizing health damage. Gallimimus has relatively low health for its torpor pool, so avoid excessive rapid-fire shots that can kill it before it falls unconscious.

As soon as it drops, access its inventory and watch the torpor meter closely. Force-feed Narcotics, Bio Toxin, or Narcoberries before the torpor gets low; Gallimimus wakes up much faster than many standard knockout tames.
