Load its inventory with Regular Kibble or your best available plant food and keep maintaining torpor throughout the tame. Once the taming bar reaches 100%, the Gallimimus will wake up fully tamed.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: High-quality Crossbow with Tranq Arrows for efficiency, or Longneck Rifle with Shocking Tranquilizer Darts for the fastest knockout.; Bring a very large supply of Narcotics or Bio Toxin. Giganotosaurus has extremely high torpor but also drains it exceptionally fast, so be ready to force-feed narcotics immediately after the knockout.

inputs.label: followed by Raw Mutton / Raw Prime Meat / Raw Meat

steps.text: Fire Tranq Arrows or Shocking Tranq Darts into the Giganotosaurus continuously. Its massive health pool can absorb the damage, so prioritize steady, accurate hits rather than spacing shots too far apart.

Keep shooting until it collapses; a Giga's torpor drains extremely quickly, so long pauses can erase a huge amount of your progress. Shocking Tranq Darts knock it out significantly faster, while a Crossbow is generally more resource-efficient.

The moment the Giga falls unconscious, access its inventory and start monitoring torpor closely. Do not assume its enormous torpor pool means you have plenty of time—the rapid drain can wake it surprisingly fast if you neglect narcotics.

Load Exceptional Kibble into its inventory and let it eat naturally while force-feeding Narcotics or Bio Toxin as needed to keep it unconscious. Continue maintaining torpor until the taming meter reaches 100%, then claim your newly tamed Giganotosaurus.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Pike, Crossbow, or another reliable weapon for killing fish; an Ichthyornis set to Hunt and Retrieve is optimal because fish it kills provide dramatically more taming progress.; No narcotics or tranquilizers required. You must physically drag dead fish corpses to the Hesperornis and interact with it while still carrying the fish.

inputs.label: then dead Coelacanth. Larger fish give substantially more taming progress
fish killed by an Ichthyornis receive a major taming bonus

steps.text: Kill a fish without harvesting its corpse, then interact with the body to drag it. Prioritize the largest Sabertooth Salmon available, or use an Ichthyornis to kill the fish for greatly increased taming progress.

While still dragging the dead fish, approach the wild Hesperornis and press the interaction key (E) when the "Feed Fish" prompt appears. The entire corpse is consumed and adds taming progress based heavily on the fish's size and species.

After each fish, there is roughly a 30-second feeding cooldown before another corpse can be given. Do not attack or knock out the Hesperornis; simply keep supplying fresh dead fish whenever the feeding prompt becomes available.

Continue killing, dragging, and feeding large fish until the taming meter reaches 100%. Using large Ichthyornis-killed fish drastically reduces the number of feeding cycles required and completes the passive tame much faster.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None required; the Hyaenodon is a passive tame and should not be damaged.; **Ghillie Armor** is strongly recommended to reduce your detection range. No food, Narcotics, or hotbar items are required for the taming interaction.

inputs.label: None; Hyaenodons are tamed entirely by **petting** rather than feeding

steps.text: Crouch before moving toward the Hyaenodon and approach carefully from behind or the side. Stay out of its immediate detection range until the **Pet** interaction prompt appears.

Press the interaction key (E) to pet the Hyaenodon and gain taming progress. After each successful pet, it will move away for a short period; remain crouched and follow without rushing directly into it.

Do not stand up, sprint into the Hyaenodon, attack nearby pack members, or let an aggressive Hyaenodon engage you. If your target becomes frightened or aggressive, you cannot pet it until it calms down, making tightly grouped packs especially difficult.

Continue stalking the Hyaenodon while crouched and pet it every time the interaction becomes available. Each successful pet increases the taming bar, and once it reaches 100%, the Hyaenodon immediately becomes yours.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Cannon with Cannon Balls; direct headshots are required to inflict meaningful torpor. A Rocket Launcher can work, but the Cannon is safer for preserving health and taming effectiveness.; Extra Cannon Balls for missed shots and Narcotics or Bio Toxin as backup torpor maintenance during slower feeding methods.

steps.text: Approach until the disguised Ice Golem rises from its resting form and becomes aggressive. Get it facing toward you so its head remains exposed for clean cannon shots.

phases.name: Hammer the Head with Cannon Balls

steps.text: Fire the Cannon directly into the Ice Golem's head. Successful headshots inflict the torpor needed for the knockout; continue landing controlled shots until its torpor climbs high enough.

Do not repeatedly hit its torso, arms, or legs—poorly placed explosive hits deal health damage without providing the necessary knockout progress and can kill the Ice Golem. Take your time between shots and make every Cannon Ball connect with the head.

Continue landing direct cannon headshots until the Ice Golem collapses unconscious. Access its inventory and load it with Extraordinary Kibble, Sulfur, Clay, or Stone, using Narcotics or Bio Toxin if necessary to keep it asleep until the tame completes.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Bola and Longneck Rifle with Tranquilizer Darts; Crossbow with Tranq Arrows works as a cheaper alternative.; Extra Bolas in case the first expires, plus Narcotics or Bio Toxin for torpor maintenance during longer tames.

inputs.label: Regular Kibble (preferred) or Raw Prime Fish Meat / Cooked Prime Fish Meat / Raw Fish Meat

steps.text: Wait for the Ichthyornis to fly low or land, then hit it with a Bola to pin it in place. Immediately switch to your tranquilizer weapon before it breaks free.

Shoot the trapped Ichthyornis with Tranq Darts or Tranq Arrows until it falls unconscious. Aim for the body rather than the head—the bird has very low health, and excessive damage can kill it before its torpor fills.

Space your tranquilizer shots and stop firing as soon as it begins going down. If the Bola expires first, follow the Ichthyornis closely; it may fly briefly before dropping unconscious once its accumulated torpor takes effect.

Once unconscious, access its inventory and load it with Regular Kibble or Raw Prime Fish Meat. Use Narcotics or Bio Toxin if its torpor falls too low, then let it eat until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Bola, Crossbow with Tranq Arrows, or preferably a Longneck Rifle with Tranquilizer Darts.; Narcotics, Bio Toxin, or Narcoberries for torpor maintenance if needed. A Bola is strongly recommended because the Iguanodon runs quickly once its torpor gets high.

steps.text: Get within throwing range and hit the Iguanodon with a Bola to stop it from sprinting away. Immediately switch to your tranq weapon while it is immobilized.
Fire Tranq Darts or Tranq Arrows into the Iguanodon until it falls unconscious. As its torpor rises, it will try to flee, so keep pressure on it before the Bola expires.
Iguanodons are fast and begin running when their health gets low or torpor gets high. Avoid unnecessary damaging shots and be ready to re-Bola it if it breaks free before the knockout.

Once unconscious, access its inventory and load it with Simple Kibble or your best available plant food. Monitor its torpor and force-feed Narcotics, Bio Toxin, or Narcoberries if necessary until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Longneck Rifle with Tranquilizer Darts or a low-damage Bow/Crossbow with Tranq Arrows. Avoid high-damage weapons; Kairuku have very low health compared with their torpor.; Narcotics, Bio Toxin, or Narcoberries for torpor maintenance. Be prepared to monitor its unconsciousness throughout the tame.

steps.text: Hit the Kairuku with Tranq Darts or carefully spaced Tranq Arrows. Once attacked, it will immediately attempt to flee rather than fight back.

Continue landing controlled tranq shots until it falls unconscious. Kairuku have low health and comparatively high torpor, so favor low-damage, high-torpor attacks and allow the delayed torpor from each shot to take effect.

phases.name: Keep It Away From the Water

steps.text: Do not let the fleeing Kairuku reach open water, where its swimming speed makes keeping up with it much harder. Most importantly, avoid unnecessary body damage or rapid-fire tranq shots that can kill it before the knockout occurs.

Once unconscious, access its inventory and load it with Basic Kibble or your best available meat. Monitor its torpor and force-feed Narcotics, Bio Toxin, or Narcoberries as needed until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Longneck Rifle with Tranq Darts (preferred) or Crossbow with Tranq Arrows; keep a Pike or Shotgun available if it grabs you.; Narcotics or Bio Toxin for torpor maintenance after knockout; a Shield can block its leap-and-grab attack while you position for tranq shots.

steps.text: Aggro the Kaprosuchus and keep it where you can clearly see its attacks. Start landing Tranq Darts or Tranq Arrows while maintaining enough distance to react to its lunges.

Let the Kaprosuchus commit to its long leap, sidestep or block it, then fire while it recovers. Its relatively low torpor makes it easier to knock out than many similarly sized predators, so steady accurate shots work quickly.

A successful leap can rip you from certain mounts and hold you in its jaws while draining stamina and dealing damage. If grabbed, fight back immediately with a melee weapon or continue tranqing it until it releases you or falls unconscious.

Continue landing tranquilizer shots until the Kaprosuchus collapses unconscious. Access its inventory and load it with Regular Kibble, Raw Mutton, or Raw Prime Meat, using Narcotics or Bio Toxin if necessary to keep its torpor above zero until the tame completes.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Longneck Rifle with Tranquilizer Darts or Shocking Tranquilizer Darts; Crossbow with Tranq Arrows works as a cheaper alternative.; Narcotics or Bio Toxin for torpor maintenance. Keep your distance and use ranged torpor weapons to avoid its reflected damage and impaling attacks.

inputs.label: Regular Kibble (preferred) or Crops / Mejoberries / other Berries

steps.text: Start landing tranquilizer shots while keeping outside the Kentrosaurus's melee reach. Maintain steady hits until its torpor begins climbing toward knockout.
Continue backing away and firing as it aggressively pursues you. Avoid using melee attacks or close-range creatures—the Kentrosaurus can reflect incoming melee damage back at its attacker.

Do not let the Kentrosaurus close the gap. Its tail attacks can impale and carry smaller targets, leaving you vulnerable and interrupting the knockout attempt; keep repositioning and continue firing from range.

Continue applying torpor until the Kentrosaurus collapses unconscious. Access its inventory, load it with Regular Kibble or Crops, and use Narcotics or Bio Toxin if its torpor drops too far before the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None required; do not attack or tranquilize the Diseased Leech.; Fish Basket. Place it on the ground underwater directly beside the Diseased Leech and allow the basket several seconds to initialize. Bug Repellant is strongly recommended to prevent the leech from targeting and attaching to you.

inputs.label: None; Diseased Leeches are captured and tamed directly with a Fish Basket

steps.text: Approach the Diseased Leech without attacking it and place a Fish Basket on the ground as close to it as possible. Wait several seconds for the basket to finish initializing before attempting the capture.

Keep the Diseased Leech close to the initialized Fish Basket until the capture interaction becomes available. Use Bug Repellant to prevent it from recognizing you as a target while you maneuver around it.

Do not allow the Diseased Leech to attach to you or another creature before capture; once a tamed leech later latches onto a target, it is permanently lost from your tame count. A wild Diseased Leech can also transmit Swamp Fever if it successfully attaches.

Look directly at the initialized Fish Basket and press the interaction key as soon as the Diseased Leech is within range. This converts it into a Filled Fish Basket; place the filled basket back down in water to release the Diseased Leech as your tame—no food, torpor, or additional feeding cycle is required.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None required; the Leech is captured rather than knocked out.; **Fish Basket**. Place it on the ground underwater near the Leech and wait a few seconds for the basket to initialize.

inputs.label: None; Leeches do not use kibble

steps.text: Set a Fish Basket on the ground close to the wild Leech and let the capture initialization finish. Keep the Leech near the basket until it becomes available for capture.

Look directly at the initialized Fish Basket and press the interaction key (E) while the Leech is within range. A successful capture converts the basket into a **Filled Fish Basket** containing the Leech.

phases.name: Do Not Let It Attach First

steps.text: Avoid letting the Leech latch onto you or another creature before capture. Once a tamed Leech later attaches to something, it is effectively a **one-time-use creature** and will permanently disappear afterward rather than returning to you.
Place the Filled Fish Basket back down in water to release the captured Leech as your tame. No knockout, feeding, or torpor maintenance is required; Fish Basket capture is the entire taming process.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None. Do not use tranquilizers or damage the Liopleurodon; it is a passive tame and may teleport away when attacked.; Place Giant Bee Honey in the very last slot of your hotbar. Approach while **dismounted**, as wild Liopleurodon can become hostile toward mounted survivors.

steps.text: Dismount your aquatic creature before closing in on the Liopleurodon. Swim directly toward it with Giant Bee Honey in your last hotbar slot and wait for the passive-feed prompt to appear.
Press the interaction key (E) to feed it Giant Bee Honey. After each feeding, remain nearby and wait for the Liopleurodon to become hungry again before giving it another piece.

Never shoot, bite, or otherwise injure the Liopleurodon during the tame; taking damage can cause it to teleport away and ruin the attempt. Stay dismounted while feeding so you do not trigger its aggression toward your mount.

Continue feeding Giant Bee Honey whenever prompted until the taming bar reaches 100%. The Liopleurodon becomes rideable without a saddle and grants its Mystic Skin Oil buff, but the creature itself is only temporarily tamed and disappears after 30 minutes.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Longneck Rifle with Tranq Darts (preferred) or Crossbow with Tranq Arrows; aim for the body rather than relying on headshots.; Narcotics or Bio Toxin for torpor maintenance after knockout; Mammoths can remain unconscious for a while, but higher levels may still require additional torpor.

steps.text: Aggro the Mammoth and begin landing Tranq Darts or Tranq Arrows while keeping enough distance to avoid its tusk attacks. Mammoths are relatively slow, making controlled kiting and steady torpor shots straightforward.
Continue firing measured tranquilizer shots as the Mammoth follows you. Maintain consistent hits until its torpor climbs high enough and it begins trying to flee.

When the Mammoth turns and runs, stay on it and keep landing tranqs without switching to damaging weapons. Avoid excessive shots once it is close to dropping so you do not waste health or accidentally kill it.

Continue tranquilizing until the Mammoth collapses unconscious. Access its inventory and load it with Superior Kibble, Crops, or Mejoberries, using Narcotics or Bio Toxin if necessary to keep it asleep until the tame completes.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None. Do not use tranquilizers or damage the Manta; it is a passive tame.; Bug Repellant (strongly recommended) and SCUBA Flippers for maneuvering. Place the AnglerGel in the very last slot of your hotbar.

steps.text: Apply Bug Repellant before swimming toward the Manta. This greatly reduces its aggression radius and allows you to get close enough to begin the passive tame without immediately being attacked.

Approach carefully from the rear with AnglerGel in your last hotbar slot. When the feeding prompt appears, press the interaction key (E) to feed it, then back away and wait until it becomes hungry again.

Do not touch the Manta's front, upper side, or underside—even with Bug Repellant active, physical contact can trigger aggression. If it attacks, retreat until it loses aggro before approaching for the next feed.

Repeat the approach-and-feed cycle every time the prompt returns until the taming bar reaches 100%. The Manta will automatically become yours with no knockout, Narcotics, or inventory-feeding phase required.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Longneck Rifle with Tranquilizer Darts or a Crossbow with Tranq Arrows; aim for the head when possible for increased torpor efficiency.; Large amounts of **Narcotics or Bio Toxin**. Megalania loses torpor extremely fast after knockout, so have your torpor supplies ready before firing the final shot.

steps.text: Attack the Megalania with tranquilizers until it drops from the wall or ceiling and begins pursuing or fleeing. Keep landing controlled tranq shots while maintaining distance.
Continue firing Tranq Darts or Tranq Arrows until the Megalania falls unconscious. Its knockout itself is straightforward, but its torpor begins draining extremely quickly once it goes down.

Access its inventory as soon as it drops and start force-feeding Narcotics or Bio Toxin before the torpor meter gets dangerously low. Do not walk away expecting a normal knockout window; a high-level Megalania can wake up very quickly if torpor maintenance is neglected.

Load its inventory with Extraordinary Kibble or your best available meat and continuously monitor torpor throughout the tame. Keep force-feeding torpor items as needed until the taming bar reaches 100% and the Megalania wakes up tamed.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Crossbow with Tranq Arrows (recommended underwater) or Harpoon Launcher with Tranq Spear Bolts.; Narcotics or Bio Toxin for torpor maintenance if needed. Bring extra tranqs because missed shots underwater are common.

inputs.label: followed by Raw Mutton / Raw Prime Meat / Raw Meat

steps.text: Shoot the Megalodon repeatedly with Tranq Arrows or Tranq Spear Bolts. Keep your shots centered on the body and maintain steady pressure as it closes the distance.
Continue firing while backing away or circling to avoid its bite attacks. Megalodons are aggressive and will usually stay committed to the chase, giving you repeated opportunities to land tranqs.

Watch for additional Megalodons joining the fight, especially if the target is part of a pack. Multiple sharks can quickly overwhelm you or kill the target through incidental combat before the knockout is complete.

Keep applying torpor until the Megalodon falls unconscious, then access its inventory and load it with Superior Kibble or meat. Use Narcotics or Bio Toxin as needed to keep it asleep until the taming meter reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Longneck Rifle with Tranquilizer Darts (preferred) or Crossbow with Tranq Arrows; use body shots for safer torpor buildup.; Narcotics or Bio Toxin for torpor maintenance, plus extra tranquilizers in case it wakes and must be knocked out again. phases.name: Knock It Out During the Day

steps.text: Engage the Megalosaurus while it is sleeping or sluggish during daylight and repeatedly hit it with Tranquilizer Darts or Arrows until it falls unconscious. Daytime is substantially safer because an awake nighttime Megalosaurus is much more aggressive.
Access its inventory and add Superior Kibble, Raw Mutton, or Raw Prime Meat. Monitor its torpor normally, but remember that Narcotics cannot prevent its special nighttime wake-up mechanic.

At approximately **20:30**, a normal Megalosaurus will wake automatically even if its torpor bar is still high. Its existing taming progress is retained, but its inventory is cleared, so immediately knock it unconscious again and replace the taming food.

Continue feeding while unconscious and re-knocking it out after any forced nighttime wake-ups until the taming bar reaches 100%. Once complete, the Megalosaurus becomes permanently yours; on Aberration, Aberrant Megalosaurus do not use the normal day/night sleep cycle.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Longneck Rifle with Tranquilizer Darts or Shocking Tranquilizer Darts; Crossbow with Tranq Arrows works as a cheaper alternative.; Narcotics or Bio Toxin for torpor maintenance. Keep plenty available, especially for higher-level Megatherium.

inputs.label: Superior Kibble (preferred) or Raw Mutton / Giant Bee Honey / Raw Prime Meat / Raw Meat

steps.text: Shoot the Megatherium with tranquilizer darts or arrows and keep landing consistent hits as it closes the distance. Aim for the head when safe for the 1.5× damage multiplier and faster torpor application.

phases.name: Watch for the Insect Killer Buff

steps.text: If the Megatherium kills an insect, it gains its powerful Insect Killer buff for 120 seconds, massively increasing its damage while reducing incoming damage by 75%. Stop engaging at close range and wait for the buff to expire before continuing the knockout.

Keep moving and maintain distance while firing; the Megatherium's bite and heavy slam can punish you quickly, especially while its insect buff is active. Do not let nearby insects trigger the buff during the knockout attempt.

Continue applying torpor until the Megatherium collapses unconscious. Access its inventory, load it with Superior Kibble or Raw Mutton, and use Narcotics or Bio Toxin as needed until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Bola followed by a Longneck Rifle with Tranq Darts or Crossbow with Tranq Arrows; Microraptors have very low health, so avoid high-damage tranq setups that could kill them.; Bola to immobilize the Microraptor, plus Narcotics or Bio Toxin only if needed for torpor maintenance after knockout.

steps.text: Approach from range and immediately hit the Microraptor with a Bola. Once restrained, keep your distance and prepare your tranquilizer weapon before it can resume its extremely fast movement.
Fire controlled Tranq Darts or Tranq Arrows until the Microraptor falls unconscious. Even while bola'd it can make short lunging attacks, so stay just outside melee range while building torpor.

Do not let an unrestrained Microraptor connect with its leap attack—it can knock you off many mounts and stun you, leaving you vulnerable while it attacks. Bola first and avoid unnecessary damaging shots because its small health pool makes accidental kills easy.

Once unconscious, access its inventory and load it with Rare Flowers or Rare Mushrooms, with Raw Mutton or Raw Prime Meat as alternatives. Monitor its rapidly draining torpor and use Narcotics or Bio Toxin if necessary until the tame completes.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None required; the Mesopithecus is a passive tame and should not be damaged.; Place your preferred food in the **last slot of your hotbar**. Crouching is strongly recommended to reduce the chance of startling it while approaching.

steps.text: Move toward the Mesopithecus while crouched and stop as soon as the feeding prompt appears. Do not move closer than necessary or it will become frightened and run away.
Press the interaction key (E) to feed it from the last slot of your hotbar. After feeding, back off slightly and follow it at a safe distance until it becomes hungry again.

phases.name: Do Not Spook or Delay It

steps.text: Avoid sprinting into the Mesopithecus or staying too close, as frightening it interrupts your ability to feed. Do not wait too long between successful feeds either, because its taming progress can slowly decrease.
Continue crouching behind the Mesopithecus and feeding it every time the interaction prompt returns. Keep the cycle consistent until the taming bar reaches 100% and the Mesopithecus becomes yours.

methods.name: Taming

inputs.label: Exceptional Kibble (preferred) or Raw Mutton / Raw Prime Meat / Raw Meat

steps.text: Engage the Mosasaurus underwater and repeatedly hit it with Tranq Arrows or Tranq Spear Bolts. Keep moving while firing and take advantage of its large turning radius to stay ahead of its bite.

Continue landing tranquilizers until its torpor becomes high enough that it attempts to flee. Stay on it and keep applying torpor; a high-level Mosasaurus can absorb a massive number of tranquilizers before finally dropping.

Do not force the Mosasaurus onto land or into water shallow enough for it to beach itself—it can die if pulled out of the water. Keep enough distance to avoid its powerful bite while maintaining consistent tranquilizer hits.

Once the Mosasaurus falls unconscious, immediately access its inventory and load it with Exceptional Kibble or meat. Monitor its torpor closely and force-feed Narcotics or Bio Toxin as needed until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None; the Moschops is a passive tame and should not be knocked out.; No narcotics or torpor items are required. Keep the food it currently requests available in your inventory and move it to the last slot of your hotbar when prompted.

inputs.label: Randomly requested food—possible requests include Sap
various berries. You must feed the exact item it requests

steps.text: Walk up to the wild Moschops and look at its passive-tame prompt. It will display one specific food it currently wants; place that exact item in the last slot of your hotbar.
Press the interaction key (E) to hand-feed the requested item. After eating, the Moschops gains taming progress and will eventually generate another random food request for the next feeding.

Check the prompt before every feed—the Moschops can switch to a completely different food each time. Do not attack or tranquilize it; damage will make the normally passive Moschops flee and can make completing the feeding sequence much harder.

Each time the Moschops becomes hungry, supply whatever specific food it requests and feed it from your last hotbar slot. Continue matching its randomized requests until the taming bar reaches 100% and the Moschops becomes yours.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Pike, Spear, Crossbow, or another precise weapon for killing fish; do not attack the Otter itself.; No Narcotics or knockout supplies required. An Ichthyornis can be used to kill fish for increased taming progress per corpse.

inputs.label: Dead fish corpses; prioritize the largest fish available
as larger fish provide substantially more taming progress

steps.text: Kill a fish without harvesting its corpse. Leave the body intact, then approach it and use the drag-body interaction to pick it up.

While physically dragging the dead fish, move close to the Otter until the **Feed Fish** prompt appears. Press the interaction key (E) while still holding the corpse to feed the entire fish and increase taming progress.

Do not accidentally strike the Otter—it has very low health and will flee when attacked. Avoid harvesting your fish before feeding them, and prioritize large fish or fish killed by an Ichthyornis for stronger progress per feeding.

Continue killing fish, dragging each intact corpse to the Otter, and feeding whenever prompted until the taming bar reaches 100%. The Otter automatically becomes yours with no knockout, Narcotics, or inventory-feeding phase required.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Bola plus a Wooden Club or Slingshot for low levels; Crossbow with Tranq Arrows or Longneck Rifle with Tranq Darts for higher levels. Oviraptors are fragile, so avoid excessive damage.; Bola to stop it from fleeing, plus Narcotics or Bio Toxin if torpor maintenance is needed after knockout.

inputs.label: followed by Quetzal Egg / Rex Egg / Spino Egg / Bronto Egg / Carno Egg / other standard or fertilized Eggs

steps.text: Hit it with a Bola before applying torpor. Oviraptors are extremely fast and will immediately flee once attacked, so immobilizing it first makes the knockout much safer.
Use a Club, Slingshot, Tranq Arrows, or Tranq Darts until it falls unconscious. Avoid high-damage headshots—the Oviraptor takes increased head damage and can die before its torpor fills.
Stop attacking the instant it collapses. Because of its low health, even one unnecessary projectile can kill it and waste the tame.

Access the unconscious Oviraptor’s inventory and load it with your best available eggs, ideally Giganotosaurus Eggs. Let it eat naturally while maintaining torpor with Narcotics or Bio Toxin as needed until the taming meter reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Bola and Wooden Club (preferred for control) or Longneck Rifle with Tranquilizer Darts; Crossbow with Tranq Arrows also works.; Extra Bolas plus Narcotics or Bio Toxin for torpor maintenance if needed. inputs.label: Simple Kibble (preferred) or Crops / Mejoberries / other Berries

steps.text: Hit the Pachy with a Bola to immobilize it before beginning the knockout. Immediately move around to its side or rear so you have a clear shot at the body.

Apply torpor with club strikes, Tranq Arrows, or Tranq Darts directly into its body. Never aim at the skull—the Pachy's reinforced headplate takes only a fraction of normal damage, making headshots extremely inefficient for knocking it out.

If the Bola expires before the knockout, stay out of the Pachy's frontal line. Its charge can rapidly close distance and inflict torpor on you, so re-Bola it or reposition before continuing your attacks.

Continue applying body shots until the Pachy collapses unconscious. Access its inventory, load it with Simple Kibble or Crops, and use Narcotics or Bio Toxin if necessary until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming

steps.text: Fire Tranq Darts or Tranq Arrows into the Pachyrhinosaurus's body, avoiding its head whenever possible. Its armored head heavily reduces incoming projectile damage, making body shots much more efficient for raising torpor.

Keep landing controlled tranquilizer shots until its torpor becomes high enough that it turns and attempts to flee. Stay on the retreating Pachyrhinosaurus and continue hitting the body until it collapses unconscious.

Move to its inventory immediately after knockout—its torpor falls exceptionally fast compared with many herbivores. Keep Narcotics or Bio Toxin ready and force-feed them before the torpor bar gets dangerously low.

Place Bug Repellant into the unconscious Pachyrhinosaurus's inventory and allow it to eat automatically as its Food decreases. Continue maintaining torpor until the taming bar reaches 100%; use Vegetables or Mejoberries only if Bug Repellant is unavailable.

methods.name: Taming

steps.text: Get within throwing range and hit the Parasaur with a Bola to stop it from fleeing. Immediately move into position before the Bola timer expires.
Shoot it with Tranq Arrows or Darts, or strike it with a Club or Slingshot, until it falls unconscious. Aim for controlled shots and stop attacking as soon as it begins to collapse.
If the Bola breaks before the knockout, the Parasaur will sprint away rather than fight. Re-bola it if possible and avoid dealing unnecessary damage that lowers taming effectiveness.
Once unconscious, access its inventory and load it with Basic Kibble, Crops, or Berries. Use Narcotics or Narcoberries if its torpor drops too low, and let it eat until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming

steps.text: Aggro the Paraceratherium and begin landing Tranq Darts or Tranq Arrows while keeping enough distance to avoid its stomp attacks. Aim for the head when you have a clean shot for the 1.5× damage multiplier.

Continue firing controlled tranqs, allowing roughly four seconds between Crossbow shots so the torpor-over-time effect can fully apply. Expect a lengthy knockout because Paraceratherium has high torpor and can move surprisingly fast for its size.

Once its torpor gets high, the Paraceratherium will attempt to flee. Stay close enough to keep landing tranqs, but avoid excessive shots once it is near unconsciousness so you do not waste health or accidentally kill it.

Continue tranquilizing until the Paraceratherium collapses unconscious. Access its inventory and load it with Superior Kibble, Crops, or Mejoberries, using Narcotics or Bio Toxin if necessary to keep its torpor above zero until the tame completes.

methods.name: Taming

steps.text: Wait until the Pelagornis is landed or within Bola range, then immobilize it before attacking. Once damaged, a wild Pelagornis immediately tries to flee, so stopping it first makes the knockout much easier.

Fire controlled Tranq Arrows or Tranq Darts until it falls unconscious. A regular Bow is especially safe because the Pelagornis has relatively low health and stronger weapons can kill it before enough torpor builds.

Do not rapidly spam high-damage tranq shots, especially headshots—the Pelagornis takes **3× headshot damage**. Allow the delayed torpor from each tranquilizer shot to build before firing unnecessarily.

Once unconscious, access its inventory and load it with Regular Kibble or Raw Prime Fish Meat. Monitor its torpor and force-feed Narcotics, Bio Toxin, or Narcoberries as needed until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming

steps.text: Get within throwing range and hit the Phiomia with a Bola before firing your tranqs. Once restrained, immediately begin the knockout before it can break free and run.

If the Bola expires before the knockout, the Phiomia will attempt to flee rather than fight. Re-bola it if possible and continue tranquilizing, avoiding unnecessary damage because its health pool is not especially large.

Continue landing tranqs until the Phiomia collapses unconscious. Access its inventory and load it with Basic Kibble, Crops, or Mejoberries, using Narcotics or Bio Toxin if necessary to keep it asleep until the tame completes.

Keep the Piranha close to the initialized basket and look directly at the basket. As soon as the capture interaction becomes available, press the interaction key (E) to trap the Piranha and convert the basket into a Filled Fish Basket.

Piranhas are aggressive and nearby individuals can quickly pile onto you while you position the basket. Do not try to knock the target unconscious—it is torpor-immune—and avoid killing it while managing the surrounding fish.

Place the Filled Fish Basket back into water to release the captured Piranha; it becomes tamed upon release. The captured Piranha keeps its original level, cannot gain experience, and requires no knockout or feeding phase.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Harpoon Launcher with Tranq Spear Bolts or Crossbow with Tranquilizer Arrows; normal firearms cannot be fired underwater.; Large supply of Bio Toxin (preferred) or Narcotics for torpor maintenance, plus SCUBA gear. steps.text: Engage the Plesiosaur underwater and repeatedly hit it with Tranq Spear Bolts or Tranq Arrows. Keep swimming while firing and use its wide turning radius to stay away from its powerful bite.

Continue applying torpor while staying above or ahead of the Plesiosaur. It tends to stop pursuing when you move too close to the surface, allowing you to reposition before dropping back down and continuing the knockout.

Do not let its large attack range catch you while reloading, and avoid getting distracted by nearby Megalodons, Dunkleosteus, Mosasaurs, or other Plesiosaurs. Losing control of the fight can force you away long enough for its rapidly draining torpor to undo your progress.

Keep landing tranquilizers until the Plesiosaur falls unconscious, then immediately access its inventory and load it with Superior Kibble or Raw Mutton. Monitor its torpor closely and force-feed Bio Toxin or Narcotics as needed until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming

inputs.label: **Rare Mushrooms** (preferred) or Plant Species X Seeds. Procoptodon will not eat normal berries or crops while wild

steps.text: Hit the Procoptodon with a Chain Bola or Net Projectile if available, then immediately begin applying torpor. If it breaks free or you lack an immobilizer, be ready to chase—it can flee extremely quickly once threatened.
Keep landing Tranq Darts or Tranq Arrows as the Procoptodon bounds away. Maintain enough stamina and distance control to keep it in sight until its torpor finally forces it unconscious.

phases.name: Do Not Use Normal Herbivore Food

steps.text: Berries, Crops, and standard herbivore kibble will not tame a wild Procoptodon. Only Rare Mushrooms and Plant Species X Seeds are accepted during the knockout tame, with Rare Mushrooms giving the better result.

steps.text: Wait for the Pteranodon to land, move within throwing range, and hit it with a Bola. Once immobilized, immediately prepare your tranquilizer weapon before it breaks free.

Once unconscious, access its inventory and load it with Regular Kibble, Raw Mutton, or Raw Prime Meat. Monitor its torpor closely and use Narcotics or Bio Toxin as needed to keep it asleep until the tame completes.

methods.name: Taming

steps.text: Watch for the small dirt mound left by a buried Purlovia and make it surface before attempting the knockout. Trigger its ambush, use an explosive nearby, or use a Yutyrannus roar to force it above ground.
Once exposed, immediately hit the Purlovia with Tranquilizer Darts or Arrows while keeping your distance. It has relatively low torpor, so sustained accurate shots will bring it down quickly.

Do not let it bury again or get a clean leap onto you; its ambush attack can stun and dismount survivors, giving it several free attacks. Keep moving and continue firing until it starts fleeing from high torpor.

Continue the tranq shots until the Purlovia collapses unconscious. Access its inventory and load it with Regular Kibble, Raw Mutton, or Raw Prime Meat, using Narcotics or Bio Toxin as needed until the taming bar reaches 100%.

inputs.label: Exceptional Kibble (preferred) or Raw Mutton / Raw Prime Meat / Raw Meat

steps.text: A wild Quetzal never lands, so you must apply torpor while following it through the air. Solo players can grapple beneath an Argentavis and whistle it toward the Quetzal, while two players can use a Tapejara with one survivor flying and the passenger firing tranquilizers.

Keep your flyer close enough for clean shots and repeatedly hit the Quetzal with Tranq Darts or Arrows as it flees. With the Argentavis method, alternate attack/move whistles to keep the bird following without letting it actually strike and damage the Quetzal.

Watch the terrain beneath the Quetzal as its torpor rises and avoid knocking it unconscious over deep water—it can fall in and drown. Stop firing immediately once it begins dropping so unnecessary damage does not reduce taming effectiveness.

Stop attacking immediately once its torpor is high enough. Jerboas have very low health, and stronger weapons or unnecessary follow-up hits can kill them before they go unconscious.
Access its inventory as soon as it drops and monitor its torpor while it eats. Jerboas wake rapidly, so force-feed Narcoberries or Narcotics if the torpor bar approaches zero.

Load Plant Species Y Seeds into its inventory for the fastest preferred tame, or use Mejoberries or other berries as alternatives. Keep it unconscious until the taming bar reaches 100%, then the Jerboa will automatically become yours.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None; the Mantis is a passive tame and should not be knocked unconscious.; Bug Repellant (required for a safe approach) and Ghillie Armor (recommended). Place the taming horn in the very last slot of your hotbar.

inputs.label: Deathworm Horn (preferred) or Woolly Rhino Horn

steps.text: Use Bug Repellant before approaching the Mantis so its aggression range is drastically reduced. Move slowly toward it without attacking or physically bumping into it.

With a Deathworm Horn or Woolly Rhino Horn in your last hotbar slot, approach close enough for the feeding prompt and press the interaction key (E). Each horn adds taming progress, after which you must wait for the Mantis to become hungry again.

Stay out of its body and avoid touching or attacking it between feeds. If the Mantis becomes aggressive or starts fighting something, taming progress can halt and may begin dropping if it remains aggroed too long.

Reapply Bug Repellant as needed and feed another horn each time the prompt becomes available. Continue the approach-feed-retreat cycle until the taming meter reaches 100% and the Mantis becomes yours.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Bola and Bow with Tranquilizer Arrows; a Longneck Rifle with Tranq Darts works but requires extra care because the Lymantria has very low health.; Extra Bolas in case it breaks free, plus Narcotics or Bio Toxin for torpor maintenance if needed.

inputs.label: Regular Kibble (preferred) or Crops / Mejoberries / other Berries

steps.text: Wait until the Lymantria is close enough to the ground, then hit it with a Bola to stop it from flying away. Immediately switch to your tranquilizer weapon and begin applying torpor.

Fire Tranq Arrows or Darts into its wings or abdomen rather than its head. Lymantria take increased projectile damage and have a massive headshot multiplier, so body shots greatly reduce the chance of killing it before the knockout.

Each time the Lymantria is attacked, it can release a green spore cloud that heavily slows movement and drains stamina. Stay outside the cloud and keep the Bola timer in mind; if it breaks free before knockout, it will attempt to fly away.

Continue carefully applying torpor until the Lymantria collapses unconscious. Access its inventory, load it with Regular Kibble or Crops, and use Narcotics or Bio Toxin if necessary until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Fire Wyvern breath (best), Flamethrower, Flame Arrows, or burning Oil Jars; only fire-based attacks increase Phoenix taming progress.; Large supply of Flamethrower Ammo or Oil Jars if not using a Fire Wyvern. No Narcotics are required because the Phoenix is not knocked unconscious.

inputs.label: None. The Phoenix is tamed entirely by repeatedly hitting it with fire; once tamed

steps.text: The Phoenix becomes available for taming only during a Scorched Earth Heat Wave. When the event begins, locate the flying Phoenix and immediately begin applying fire damage.

Hit the Phoenix repeatedly with Fire Wyvern breath, a Flamethrower, Flame Arrows, or burning Oil Jars. Each successful fire hit increases taming progress, with Fire Wyvern breath providing one of the fastest and most effective methods.

Maintain frequent fire hits so taming effectiveness does not drop and finish before the Heat Wave ends. If time expires, the Phoenix disintegrates into an ash pile and will respawn from the same ashes during the next Heat Wave with its taming progress preserved.
Continue bathing the Phoenix in fire until the taming meter reaches 100%. It becomes immediately tamed with no knockout or feeding stage; place Sulfur in its inventory afterward when it needs food.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Cannon with Cannon Balls (preferred); Rocket Launcher works but is far less efficient and risks killing the Rock Elemental.; Plenty of Cannon Balls, plus Narcotics or Bio Toxin only if needed for torpor maintenance after knockout.

steps.text: Approach the disguised boulder until the Rock Elemental emerges and becomes aggressive. Position yourself so you have a clear, consistent shot at its head.

Fire Cannon Balls directly into the Rock Elemental's head; successful torpor hits cause a distinct head-shaking animation. Cannon Balls deal massive torpor, while body shots add little or no torpor and instead inflict dangerous health damage.

Do not spam explosives into its torso or legs—the Rock Elemental can die before reaching knockout if your shots miss the head. Wait for clean firing angles and confirm the head-shake reaction before committing the next Cannon Ball.

Continue landing Cannon Ball headshots until the Rock Elemental collapses unconscious. Access its inventory and load it with Extraordinary Kibble, Sulfur, Clay, or Stone, maintaining torpor if necessary until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Longneck Rifle with Tranquilizer Darts or Shocking Tranquilizer Darts; Crossbow with Tranq Arrows works as a cheaper alternative.; Narcotics or Bio Toxin for torpor maintenance if needed. Bring extra tranquilizers for higher-level Thorny Dragons and keep enough distance to avoid their ranged spine attacks.

inputs.label: Regular Kibble (preferred) or Raw Mutton / Raw Prime Meat / Cooked Lamb Chop / Raw Meat

steps.text: Shoot the Thorny Dragon with Tranq Darts or Arrows while maintaining distance. Keep landing controlled shots as it pursues you; once its health or torpor gets high enough, it will eventually turn and attempt to flee.
Watch for the Thorny Dragon to fire a burst of tail spines at range. Strafe sideways or duck behind cover when it attacks—the projectiles inflict torpor and can quickly disrupt your knockout attempt.

Once the Thorny Dragon starts running, immediately follow and continue landing tranquilizers. Do not let it gain too much distance or disappear over cliffs or rough terrain while its torpor continues draining.

Continue applying torpor until the Thorny Dragon collapses unconscious. Access its inventory, load it with Regular Kibble or Raw Mutton, and use Narcotics or Bio Toxin as needed until the taming bar reaches 100%.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: None; the Vulture is a passive tame and should not be knocked unconscious.; Ghillie Armor and Cactus Broth are recommended to reduce detection. Place the taming food in the very last slot of your hotbar.

steps.text: Move toward the Vulture carefully with Spoiled Meat in your last hotbar slot. Do not attack it or approach while it is already fighting something; this is a non-violent passive tame.
When the interaction prompt appears, press the interaction key (E) to feed it. Back away afterward and follow it as necessary until it becomes hungry enough for the next feed.

Do not kill nearby creatures during the tame—a corpse can immediately trigger the Vulture's aggression and interrupt or reset your progress. If something attacks you, knocking it unconscious instead of killing it avoids creating a corpse that could ruin the tame.
Continue approaching and feeding Spoiled Meat every time the prompt becomes available. Repeat the feed-and-wait cycle until the taming meter reaches 100% and the Vulture becomes yours.

methods.name: Taming
methods.requirements: Longneck Rifle with Tranquilizer Darts or Crossbow with Tranq Arrows for knocking out a **female Wyvern to harvest Wyvern Milk**; adult Wyverns themselves cannot be tamed.; **Fertilized Wyvern Egg** and enough heat or insulation to maintain roughly **80–90°C / 176–194°F** for incubation. Air Conditioners, Dimetrodons, or other strong incubation sources work.

inputs.label: **Wyvern Milk** for the baby until adulthood. In ASA on Ragnarok
**Bison Milk** can also raise Wyverns when its requirement is met

steps.text: Adult Fire, Lightning, Poison, and Ice Wyverns cannot be domesticated directly; you must steal a fertilized egg from a wild nest. Taking the egg immediately provokes nearby wild Wyverns, so secure the egg and escape without trying to tame the adults.
Place the egg in enough heat or insulation to maintain approximately **80–90°C / 176–194°F**. Keep the temperature stable until incubation finishes and the baby Wyvern hatches.

Knock out a **wild female Wyvern** and take the Wyvern Milk from her inventory, or kill an Alpha Wyvern for a larger supply. Newly hatched Wyverns do not normally eat Raw Meat and rely on milk while growing, so have it available before the baby's Food becomes critical.

Claim the newborn and feed it Wyvern Milk as needed while completing its maturation and imprinting requests. Once it reaches adulthood, it begins accepting normal meat and becomes your fully usable tamed Wyvern with no saddle required.

methods.requirements: High-damage Pump-Action Shotgun, Fabricated Sniper Rifle, or powerful combat tames capable of killing the Dodo Wyvern and surviving its Zombie Wyvern escorts.; None; Zombie Fire Wyverns are claimed rather than knocked out or fed. No saddle is required once claimed.

inputs.label: None; Zombie Fire Wyverns have no conventional taming food

steps.text: Kill the Dodo Wyvern while avoiding or surviving the Zombie Wyverns accompanying it. Do not waste Tranq Arrows or Tranq Darts on the Zombie Fire Wyvern itself—the normal acquisition mechanic is tied directly to defeating the Dodo Wyvern.
The moment the Dodo Wyvern dies, every wild Zombie Wyvern currently on the map becomes claimable, including Zombie Fire Wyverns. They no longer require combat, torpor, or feeding to domesticate.

Once the boss is dead, stop attacking the Zombie Fire Wyvern you want. Continuing to damage it can kill your newly available tame before you reach it, especially if multiple players or creatures are still attacking nearby targets.
Approach the now-claimable Zombie Fire Wyvern and press the interaction key (E) to claim it. Ownership transfers immediately—there is no knockout, feeding, maturation, or saddle step required.

Zombie Lightning Wyverns become directly claimable after the Dodo Wyvern is defeated. No Narcotics, tranqs, saddle, or incubation supplies are required.

inputs.label: None. The Zombie Lightning Wyvern uses a post-boss claiming mechanic rather than knockout

steps.text: Kill the event’s Dodo Wyvern using your strongest combat creatures and weapons. Zombie Wyverns normally spawn alongside the Dodo Wyvern and remain hostile until the boss is defeated.

The instant the Dodo Wyvern dies, **all wild Zombie Wyverns on the map become claimable**, including Zombie Lightning Wyverns that were not directly accompanying the boss. No torpor or feeding phase is required.

Locate the Zombie Lightning Wyvern you want and approach once the Dodo Wyvern has been defeated. Do not kill it during the boss fight if you intend to keep it; once claimable, its normal hostile behavior is replaced by the claim interaction.
Walk up to the claimable Zombie Lightning Wyvern and press the interaction key (E) to claim it. It immediately becomes your tame, requires no saddle to ride, and cannot be bred.

steps.text: Kill the active Dodo Wyvern with your strongest combat tames and weapons. This is the trigger that unlocks the Zombie Wyverns for claiming.
Once the Dodo Wyvern dies, **all wild Zombie Wyverns on the map become claimable**, including Zombie Poison Wyverns—even ones that did not spawn directly beside the boss.

Stop attacking the Zombie Poison Wyvern after the boss dies and approach it carefully. There is no torpor or feeding phase; continuing to fight it only risks killing the creature you are trying to obtain.

Move into interaction range and press the interaction key (E) to claim the Zombie Poison Wyvern directly. It becomes immediately rideable with no saddle, knockout, raising, or feeding process required.
